## Why

In `etl/manager_similarity_flow.py:27-47`, the function `ensure_manager_similarity_table(conn)` executes table creation DDL only when `isinstance(conn, sqlite3.Connection)`.

When executed against a PostgreSQL connection, `ensure_manager_similarity_table(conn)` executes no statements and provides no fallback or table verification. This inconsistency contrasts with all other table ensure functions across the codebase (such as `etl/conviction_flow.py`, `alerts/db.py`, and `etl/activism_detection.py`), which provide PostgreSQL DDL branches.

## Scope

- Implement PostgreSQL DDL execution in `ensure_manager_similarity_table()` in `etl/manager_similarity_flow.py:27-47` matching dialect patterns used across `etl/`.
- Add test coverage in `tests/test_manager_similarity_flow.py` verifying table creation DDL execution on PostgreSQL connections.

## Implementation Notes

- Mirror the PostgreSQL table creation schema in `etl/conviction_flow.py` using `BIGINT`, `TIMESTAMPTZ`, and `FLOAT` types.
- Ensure idempotent execution using `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS manager_similarity (...)`.

## Non-Goals

- Modifying similarity computation algorithms or vector embedding distance metrics.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add PostgreSQL dialect DDL branch to function `ensure_manager_similarity_table()` in `etl/manager_similarity_flow.py`.
- [ ] Add test cases in `tests/test_manager_similarity_flow.py` asserting PostgreSQL DDL executes on non-SQLite connection instances.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_manager_similarity_flow.py` executes without errors.
- Calling `ensure_manager_similarity_table(pg_conn)` on a PostgreSQL mock connection executes DDL creating table `manager_similarity`.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by omitting PostgreSQL handling in `etl/manager_similarity_flow.py` and verify `pytest tests/test_manager_similarity_flow.py` fails.
title: fix(etl): implement Postgres schema check in ensure_manager_similarity_table

## Why

In `adapters/prices.py:231-245`, the method `close_on_or_before(symbol, on)` evaluates `needs_refresh = not window or max(window) < on` to determine whether an external market data fetch is required.

When requesting market prices for a non-trading date (such as a weekend Saturday or Sunday), `max(window) < on` remains True even after fetching because markets are closed on `on`. Because `window` contains Friday's quote (non-empty), `(symbol, on)` is never added to `self._missing`. On subsequent calls for the same symbol and weekend date, `needs_refresh` evaluates to True again, triggering redundant external HTTP network requests on every invocation.

## Scope

- Update `close_on_or_before()` in `adapters/prices.py:231-245` to record evaluated `(symbol, on)` dates in a refreshed/checked set once a lookup window has been queried.
- Add unit test coverage in `tests/test_adapter_base.py` asserting that repeated calls to `close_on_or_before()` for non-trading weekend dates do not trigger duplicate network fetches.

## Implementation Notes

- Track queried date windows using `self._checked_dates: set[tuple[str, date]] = set()`.
- If `(symbol, on)` has already been evaluated and the cache contains the latest available quote before `on`, skip redundant network calls.

## Non-Goals

- Modifying external market data provider endpoints or rate limiter throttling logic.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement checked date caching in method `close_on_or_before()` in `adapters/prices.py` to prevent redundant network fetches on non-trading dates.
- [ ] Add unit test in `tests/test_adapter_base.py` verifying that multiple lookups for weekend dates invoke the mock provider exactly once.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_adapter_base.py` executes without errors.
- Querying `close_on_or_before("AAPL", saturday_date)` multiple times results in exactly 1 call to the underlying provider fetch method.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by removing the checked date cache in `adapters/prices.py` and verify `pytest tests/test_adapter_base.py` fails on redundant call assertions.
title: fix(prices): eliminate redundant HTTP requests for weekend and holiday dates in PriceAdapter

## Why

In `api/activism.py:195, 255, 365, 432, 515`, query functions (`query_activism_filings`, `query_activism_events`, `query_active_campaigns`, `query_activism_timeline`, `query_manager_campaigns`) execute SQL containing `LEFT JOIN managers m ON m.manager_id = ...`.

In SQLite databases where table `managers` defines primary key column `id` (standard across local SQLite schemas), executing any of these activism queries raises `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: m.manager_id`, breaking activism API endpoints in local development and offline inspection workflows.

## Scope

- Resolve the manager table join column dynamically in `api/activism.py:195, 255, 365, 432, 515` using dialect helper `manager_id_column(conn)` or `resolve_manager_id_column(conn)`.
- Add test coverage in `tests/test_activism_dialect_portability.py` executing activism queries against SQLite databases where table `managers` has column `id`.

## Implementation Notes

- Use `manager_id_column(conn)` or `resolve_manager_id_column(conn)` to dynamically format `LEFT JOIN managers m ON m.{manager_col} = ...`.
- Ensure parameter bindings remain parameterized and only the validated column identifier is formatted into the SQL clause.

## Non-Goals

- Changing activism endpoint schemas or modifying PostgreSQL schema definitions.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update SQL query templates in `api/activism.py` to resolve dialect-specific manager column names in table joins.
- [ ] Add regression tests in `tests/test_activism_dialect_portability.py` executing activism queries against SQLite connections with `id` PK columns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_activism_dialect_portability.py` executes without errors.
- Query functions in `api/activism.py` return valid records when queried against SQLite schemas without raising `OperationalError`.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by hardcoding `m.manager_id` in `api/activism.py` joins and verify `pytest tests/test_activism_dialect_portability.py` fails on SQLite schemas.
title: fix(api-activism): resolve SQLite column error for managers table join in activism queries

## Why

In `alerts/models.py:33-35`, the rule condition `similar_manager_count_gte` is listed in `_NUMERIC_CONDITION_BOUNDS` as a floating-point number with range `(1.0, None)`, rather than in `_INTEGER_CONDITION_KEYS` alongside `manager_count_gte` and `news_count_gt`.

Because `similar_manager_count_gte` represents a discrete count of similar investment managers, fractional values such as `2.5` should be rejected during validation. Furthermore, in `alerts/engine.py:100-105`, event payload matching evaluates `_as_int(payload.get("similar_manager_count"))` while comparing against `_as_float(expected)`.

## Scope

- Move `similar_manager_count_gte` to `_INTEGER_CONDITION_KEYS` in `alerts/models.py:33-35` and set integer lower bound `similar_manager_count_gte: (1, None)`.
- Update threshold extraction in function `evaluate_rule()` in `alerts/engine.py:100-105` to parse discrete count thresholds.
- Add test cases in `tests/test_alert_engine.py` verifying that fractional values for `similar_manager_count_gte` raise validation errors.

## Implementation Notes

- In `alerts/models.py`, add `"similar_manager_count_gte"` to `_INTEGER_CONDITION_KEYS` and `_INTEGER_CONDITION_BOUNDS = {"similar_manager_count_gte": (1, None)}`.
- In `alerts/engine.py`, ensure count condition evaluation checks integer thresholds consistently across event evaluation flows.

## Non-Goals

- Modifying threshold bounds for continuous financial metrics such as `value_usd_gt` or `pct_change_gte`.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Relocate `similar_manager_count_gte` to integer condition collections in `alerts/models.py`.
- [ ] Align rule evaluation in function `evaluate_rule()` in `alerts/engine.py` to parse count thresholds as integers.
- [ ] Add test cases in `tests/test_alert_engine.py` validating that fractional threshold configurations are rejected with validation errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Constructing `AlertRuleCreate(name="test", event_type="similarity_cluster", conditions={"similar_manager_count_gte": 2.5})` raises `ValueError`.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by allowing float inputs for `similar_manager_count_gte` in `alerts/models.py` and verify `pytest tests/test_alert_engine.py` fails.
title: fix(alerts): enforce integer validation for similar_manager_count_gte rule condition

## Why

In `ui/upload.py:43-44`, the function `_load_managers(conn)` executes SQL `SELECT manager_id, name FROM managers ORDER BY name ASC`.

On SQLite database instances created via `_ensure_manager_table()` or `scripts/seed_managers.py`, the primary key column on table `managers` is named `id`, not `manager_id`. Executing `_load_managers(conn)` raises `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: manager_id`, which is caught by the exception block, causing `_load_managers(conn)` to silently return an empty list `[]` and rendering the manager selector empty during manual filing uploads.

## Scope

- Update `_load_managers()` in `ui/upload.py:43-44` to resolve the manager primary key column dynamically using `resolve_manager_id_column(conn)` from `adapters.base`.
- Add test coverage in `tests/test_upload.py` ensuring `_load_managers()` successfully loads manager records from SQLite databases with `id` column schemas.

## Implementation Notes

- Use `from adapters.base import resolve_manager_id_column` in `ui/upload.py` to dynamically construct `SELECT {id_col}, name FROM managers ORDER BY name ASC`.
- Verify exception handling logs unexpected database errors while keeping graceful empty list fallbacks for uninitialized databases.

## Non-Goals

- Refactoring CSV or PDF parsing pipelines in `ui/upload.py`.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Import `resolve_manager_id_column` and update SQL column resolution in function `_load_managers()` in `ui/upload.py`.
- [ ] Add regression test in `tests/test_upload.py` verifying `_load_managers()` queries SQLite tables configured with `id` primary keys.

## Why

In `ui/alerts.py:75-80`, the helper function `_load_managers(api_url)` queries `GET /managers` and filters the returned items using `if item.get("id") is not None and item.get("name")` to extract `(int(item["id"]), str(item["name"]))`.

The API endpoint `GET /managers` (defined in `api/managers.py:48-62`) returns manager entities serialized with field name `manager_id`, not `id`. As a result, `item.get("id")` is always `None`, causing `_load_managers()` to discard all managers and return an empty list `[]`. Consequently, the manager selector dropdown in the alert creation and subscription interface remains completely empty.

## Scope

- Update `_load_managers()` in `ui/alerts.py:75-80` to retrieve the manager identifier via `item.get("manager_id") or item.get("id")`.
- Add test coverage in `tests/test_ui_alerts.py` to verify that `_load_managers()` parses manager dictionaries containing `manager_id`.

## Implementation Notes

- In `ui/alerts.py`, support both `item.get("manager_id")` and `item.get("id")` to maintain backward and forward compatibility with various backend manager schemas.
- Ensure manager integer conversion handles valid string or integer IDs safely.

## Non-Goals

- Modifying alert channel notifications or altering alert rule dispatch logic in `alerts/engine.py`.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update manager ID resolution in function `_load_managers()` in `ui/alerts.py` to accept `manager_id` keys from API payloads.
- [ ] Add regression test in `tests/test_ui_alerts.py` asserting `_load_managers()` returns manager ID and name tuples when given `manager_id` responses.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_ui_alerts.py` executes without errors.
- Invoking `_load_managers()` with API payload `[{"manager_id": 1, "name": "Elliott"}]` returns `[(1, "Elliott")]`.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by requiring `item["id"]` in `ui/alerts.py` and confirm `pytest tests/test_ui_alerts.py` fails.
title: fix(alerts-ui): fix manager selector empty list caused by manager_id key mismatch

body:
## Why

In `ui/dashboard.py:50-55`, the helper function `load_delta(engine)` executes SQL `SELECT filed as date, COUNT(*) AS filings FROM holdings GROUP BY filed ORDER BY filed`.

The `holdings` table schema does not possess a column named `filed` (filing dates are stored in `filings.filed_date` or as timestamp metadata in `holdings.knowledge_time` / `holdings.created_at`). When a user accesses the dashboard and expands the `Historical Filing Trend` section in `ui/dashboard.py:1184`, the database query raises `pandas.errors.DatabaseError: Execution failed on sql ...: no such column: filed`, causing the Streamlit application to crash at runtime.

## Scope

- Update the SQL query in function `load_delta()` in `ui/dashboard.py:50-55` to query `filings.filed_date` from the `filings` table (or join `holdings` to `filings` on `filing_id` when grouping by filing date).
- Add regression testing in `tests/test_dashboard.py` verifying that `load_delta()` executes successfully against database engines with valid filing records.

## Implementation Notes

- In `ui/dashboard.py`, `load_delta(engine)` can query `SELECT filed_date as date, COUNT(*) AS filings FROM filings GROUP BY filed_date ORDER BY filed_date`.
- Ensure column aliasing produces `date` and `filings` columns so downstream plotting in `ui/dashboard.py` functions without modifications.

## Non-Goals

- Redesigning dashboard chart visualizations or altering other summary metrics in `ui/dashboard.py`.
- Adding scaffold-only stubs, mocks, or empty bypass functions without wiring up the real implementation does NOT count as done and constitutes a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update SQL query in function `load_delta()` in `ui/dashboard.py` to aggregate filing dates from `filings.filed_date` instead of table `holdings`.
- [ ] Add regression test in `tests/test_dashboard.py` asserting `load_delta()` executes without SQL syntax or column errors and returns grouped counts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `pytest tests/test_dashboard.py` executes without errors.
- Invoking `load_delta(engine)` against a seeded database returns a DataFrame containing `date` and `filings` columns.
- Verification gate: deliberately break the implementation by referencing `holdings.filed` in `ui/dashboard.py` and confirm `pytest tests/test_dashboard.py` fails with a database missing column error.
title: fix(dashboard): resolve crash in load_delta on missing filed column

## Why

This is a current break: `etl/activism_flow.py:346-355` catches every `materialize_activism_campaigns` exception, logs it, and returns rows; `etl/activism_flow.py:358-367` then logs "Activism flow finished" and returns successfully. `api/activism.py:392-433` reads the derived `activism_campaigns` table, so a failed materialization leaves campaign endpoints stale or absent while the scheduler sees a successful ingestion.

## Scope

Make the campaign-materialization stage visible to the flow's success or failure result while retaining committed filing records.

## Implementation Notes

Close the materialization connection in `finally`, then propagate the captured exception or return an explicit failed flow contract. Do not roll back already committed source filing data solely because a derived rebuild failed; the required change is truthful run status and retry eligibility.

## Tasks

- [x] Update `etl/activism_flow.py` so a campaign materialization exception escapes after connection cleanup.
- [x] Extend `tests/test_activism_adapter.py` with an injected materialization exception from `fetch_all_managers`.
- [x] Extend `tests/test_activism_campaign_flow.py` only if a helper-level regression fixture is needed to exercise the derived contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

`pytest tests/test_activism_adapter.py tests/test_activism_campaign_flow.py -q` passes, including `tests/test_activism_adapter.py::test_fetch_all_managers_propagates_campaign_materialization_failure`, and a simulated failure does not report a successful result. Temporarily reintroduce `except Exception: logger.exception(...); return rows` and confirm `tests/test_activism_adapter.py::test_fetch_all_managers_propagates_campaign_materialization_failure` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

Do not change campaign scoring, filing de-duplication, or historical campaign records in this issue.

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: logging a materialization exception while returning a successful ingestion result is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] Fail activism ingestion when campaign materialization fails

- [x] Extend `tests/test_ingest_flow.py` with an explicit-`db_path` ingestion case that captures document storage arguments.

## Why

This is a current latent break: `api/chat.py:1283-1286` and `api/chat.py:1501-1541` call raw `float()` and only upper-clamp timeout values. `api/chat.py:1419-1428` passes those values into the health summary, and `api/chat.py:1583-1585` uses them as an asyncio deadline. `nan`, negative, or malformed deployment values therefore propagate as invalid budgets or raise from a health endpoint.

## Scope

Validate all health-summary, dependency-probe, and circuit-reset timeout environment values at their parsing boundary.

## Implementation Notes

Use a shared small helper in `api/chat.py` or `utils/numeric.py` that accepts only finite positive floats, applies each existing upper cap, and falls back to the documented default on invalid input. Preserve the established normal-value caps and defaults.

## Tasks

- [x] Update `api/chat.py` so health timeout and circuit-reset environment parsing rejects non-finite, non-positive, and malformed values through documented defaults.
- [x] Extend `tests/test_db_health.py` with database timeout configuration cases for invalid numeric values.
- [x] Extend `tests/test_app_health.py` with summary-budget cases that exercise the health endpoint rather than only a parser helper.
- [x] Extend `tests/test_health_detailed.py` with invalid MinIO and Redis timeout configuration cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

`pytest tests/test_db_health.py tests/test_app_health.py tests/test_health_detailed.py -q` passes and each supported timeout source falls back to a finite positive value for `nan`, infinity, zero, negative, and nonnumeric input. Temporarily return `float(os.environ["DB_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_S"])` without validation and confirm `tests/test_db_health.py::test_health_db_invalid_timeout_configuration_uses_default` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

Do not alter dependency retry counts, network endpoints, or normal configured timeout caps.

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: parsing only one timeout environment variable while another health path still accepts an invalid budget is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] Make health probe timeout configuration finite and positive

## Why

`alerts/db.py:20-25` redefines `is_sqlite` and `placeholder` while `adapters/base.py:100-112` already exposes `is_sqlite` and `get_placeholder` with identical semantics. `alerts/db.py:78-92` also duplicates the `_sqlite_columns` / `_sqlite_add_column_if_missing` pattern found in `adapters/openfigi.py:219-223`. This is a **latent** consolidation gap — two placeholder naming conventions (`placeholder` vs `get_placeholder`) increase the chance of dialect bugs when editing alert SQL. No current runtime break verified.

## Scope

- `alerts/db.py` — remove local dialect helpers; import from `adapters/base.py`.
- All `alerts/` modules that import from `alerts.db` — unchanged public API (`placeholder` call sites become `get_placeholder` internally).

## Implementation Notes

- Replace `placeholder(conn)` calls with `get_placeholder(conn)` throughout `alerts/db.py`.
- `_sqlite_columns` can be replaced by `get_table_columns` from `adapters/base.py` where the return type (`set[str]`) matches usage in `_sqlite_add_column_if_missing`.
- Keep `ensure_alert_tables` DDL strings unchanged; this is import consolidation only.

## Tasks

- [x] Remove `is_sqlite` and `placeholder` from `alerts/db.py` and import `is_sqlite`, `get_placeholder`, `get_table_columns` from `adapters/base.py`.
- [x] Refactor `_sqlite_add_column_if_missing` in `alerts/db.py` to use `get_table_columns` instead of local `_sqlite_columns`.
- [x] Run `pytest tests/test_alert_engine.py tests/test_alerts_api.py` and fix any import fallout in `alerts/engine.py` if it imported `placeholder` by name.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/test_alert_engine.py tests/test_alerts_api.py` passes on the fixed tree.
- Deliberate-break: temporarily restore a local `placeholder` returning the wrong marker for Postgres in `alerts/db.py` and confirm `pytest tests/test_alerts_api.py::test_alert_rule_create_rejects_non_finite_numeric_condition` or another Postgres-path alert test fails; revert before merge.

## Why

`alerts/models.py:27-34` lists `_NUMERIC_CONDITION_BOUNDS` for float keys but omits `news_count_gt` and `manager_count_gte`. `validate_condition_json` (`alerts/models.py:60-77`) only validates keys in that map, so `{"news_count_gt": "nan"}` passes create/update validation unchanged. `alerts/engine.py:81-84` then calls `int(expected)`, which raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'nan'` during `AlertEngine.evaluate`. Reproduced on current tip with a direct DB insert. This is a **latent break** — evaluation crashes instead of rejecting the rule at persistence time. `tests/test_alerts_api.py:210-220` only covers float keys like `value_usd_gt`.

## Scope

- `alerts/models.py` — extend `validate_condition_json` for integer count keys.
- `alerts/engine.py` — replace bare `int(expected)` with safe parsing for `news_count_gt` and `manager_count_gte` (defense in depth).
- `tests/test_alerts_api.py` — reject invalid integer conditions at POST/PUT.
- `tests/test_alert_engine.py` — optional engine-level test for DB-seeded invalid rules if API bypass exists.

## Implementation Notes

- Integer keys should require a positive integer (`>= 1` for `news_count_gt`, `>= 1` for `manager_count_gte` per engine semantics).
- Reject non-integer strings, floats with fractional parts, `nan`, and `inf` at validation time with the same `ValueError` message pattern as float keys.
- `similar_manager_count_gte` is already in `_NUMERIC_CONDITION_BOUNDS`; do not regress its behavior.

## Tasks

- [x] Add integer validation for `news_count_gt` and `manager_count_gte` in `alerts/models.py::validate_condition_json`.
- [x] Replace bare `int(expected)` with `_as_int` (or equivalent) for count keys in `alerts/engine.py::_evaluate_condition`.
- [x] Add `tests/test_alerts_api.py::test_alert_rule_create_rejects_invalid_news_count_gt` posting `{"news_count_gt": "nan"}` and expecting HTTP 400 with `Invalid numeric alert condition`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/test_alerts_api.py::test_alert_rule_create_rejects_invalid_news_count_gt` passes on the fixed tree.
- Deliberate-break: temporarily remove the new integer validation block from `alerts/models.py` and confirm `pytest tests/test_alerts_api.py::test_alert_rule_create_rejects_invalid_news_count_gt` fails; revert before merge.

## Non-Goals

- Do not redesign alert event types or delivery channels.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding a comment in `alerts/engine.py` without API rejection and a failing regression test is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] Validate integer alert condition keys at API boundary

## Why

`api/signals.py:88-94` defines `_to_float` as a bare `float()` cast with no `math.isfinite` guard. The parallel helper in `api/activism.py:110-118` already documents and handles the case: *"SQLite REAL columns can hold Infinity/NaN, which Starlette cannot serialize."* Reproduced on current tip: a `crowded_trades` row with `total_value_usd=Infinity` flows through `query_crowded_trades` and `JSONResponse` raises `ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: inf`. This is a **current break** for `/api/signals/*` when polluted REAL data exists; activism endpoints on the same database return `null` instead of 500.

## Scope

- `api/signals.py` — `_to_float` and all call sites that serialize signal payloads (`CrowdedTradeResponse`, `ContrarianSignalResponse`, `ConvictionScoreResponse`, `ManagerAttributionResponse`).
- `tests/test_signals_api.py` — new regression test mirroring `tests/test_activism_api.py::test_campaign_query_drops_non_finite_ownership`.

## Implementation Notes

- Reuse `utils/numeric.py::finite_float_or_none` (already imported elsewhere in the API layer) instead of maintaining a third `_to_float` variant.
- Do not change response field types; map non-finite inputs to `None` like activism does.
- `tests/test_signals_api.py` already seeds crowded/contrarian/conviction tables; extend with a row whose REAL column is `1e999` (SQLite stores as Infinity).

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace `api/signals.py::_to_float` with `finite_float_or_none` from `utils/numeric.py` and delete the local helper.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_signals_api.py::test_crowded_trades_drops_non_finite_values` asserting `query_crowded_trades` returns `total_value_usd is None` for an Infinity row and the HTTP GET `/api/signals/crowded` returns 200 with `null` in JSON.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/test_signals_api.py::test_crowded_trades_drops_non_finite_values` passes on the fixed tree.
- Deliberate-break: temporarily remove the `isfinite` guard (restore bare `float()` in `api/signals.py`) and confirm `pytest tests/test_signals_api.py::test_crowded_trades_drops_non_finite_values` fails; revert before merge.

## Non-Goals

- Do not refactor `api/activism.py` or other modules in this change.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: leaving `_to_float` as bare `float()` while only adding a test comment is a failure of this issue.
title: [P1] Signals API must reject non-finite REAL values before JSON encoding

body:
## Why (verified evidence)

MgrDB's production Research-chat path resolves LLM models through a repo-local, **fail-OPEN** client that ignores the model registry's `lifecycle` and reviewed `selections`. A model the registry marks ineligible can therefore silently become the serving model. The fleet's hardened **fail-CLOSED** resolver is present in this repo but unreachable on that path.

- `api/chat.py:501-519` — `_build_chat_client_info()` calls `importlib.import_module("llm.client")` at `:505` and returns `build_fn()` at `:514` whenever that import succeeds. `llm/client.py` exists in this repo, so the import **always** succeeds and the `from tools.langchain_client import build_chat_client` fallback at `:517-519` is unreachable dead code.
- `llm/client.py:87-123` (`_load_slot_config`), `:126-157` (`_apply_slot_env_overrides`), `:228-268` (`build_chat_client`) — every eligibility gate is `is_model_blocked(...)` alone (`:118`, `:142`, `:246`, `:257`, `:262`). Neither `lifecycle` nor the registry's reviewed `selections` is consulted, so a model **absent** from the registry, or present with `lifecycle != "current"`, is allowed through.
- `llm/client.py:73-77` — `_default_slots()` hardcodes model version literals, including `SlotDefinition(name="slot2", provider="anthropic", model="claude-sonnet-4-6")` at `:76`. That `model_id` does **not** exist in `config/model_registry.json` (verified). By contrast the synced resolver builds defaults "from registry decisions, never version constants" (`tools/llm_registry.py:318`).
- **Reproduction** (real repo registry, no env registry override): with `LANGCHAIN_SLOT_CONFIG` pointing at `{"slots":[{"name":"s1","provider":"openai","model":"gpt-5.5"}]}` and `MANAGER_DB_OPENAI_API_KEY` set — `llm.client.build_chat_client()` **serves `gpt-5.5`**, while for identical input `tools.llm_registry.resolve_slots()` returns `[]` and `configured_model_for_provider("openai")` returns `""`. `config/model_registry.json` records `gpt-5.5` as `lifecycle: "compatibility"` with the note *"It is not eligible for auxiliary evaluator selection."*

**Consequence:** a deprecated or registry-ineligible model can remain the primary serving model on the chat path without tripping any gate — the exact failure mode `stranske/Workflows#2710` (registry-as-source-of-truth so old models don't stay primary) exists to prevent.

**Scope of severity:** this is a governance/drift gap, **not** user-exploitable. It requires control of deployment configuration (`LANGCHAIN_SLOT_CONFIG`, `LANGCHAIN_MODEL`, `LANGCHAIN_SLOT{n}_MODEL`), not user input. The explicit `blocked: true` guard itself works correctly (verified separately); this issue is about **non-current and registry-absent** models only.

## Tasks

- [ ] `llm/client.py:87-123` — in `_load_slot_config`, reject a slot whose model is absent from the registry or whose entry has `lifecycle != "current"`, in addition to the existing `is_model_blocked` check at `:118`.
- [ ] `llm/client.py:126-157` — apply the same eligibility check to `_apply_slot_env_overrides` so `LANGCHAIN_SLOT{n}_MODEL` / `LANGCHAIN_MODEL` cannot introduce a non-current model (currently gated only at `:142`).
- [ ] `llm/client.py:228-268` — apply the same check to the explicit-provider path in `build_chat_client` at `:243-249`, where `model or LANGCHAIN_MODEL or _default_slots()[0].model` is gated only by `is_model_blocked` at `:246`.
- [ ] `llm/client.py:73-77` — replace the hardcoded `_default_slots()` literals with registry-derived defaults (delegate to `tools.llm_registry.default_slots()`), eliminating `claude-sonnet-4-6` at `:76`, which is absent from `config/model_registry.json`.
- [ ] `api/chat.py:517-519` — remove the unreachable `tools.langchain_client` fallback, or make `_build_chat_client_info()` actually prefer the synced resolver. Do not leave two client paths with one silently dead.
- [ ] Update the three tests that deliberately pin the pre-hardening fail-open behavior so they assert the hardened contract — these are intentional existing expectations, **not** regressions to preserve: `tests/test_llm_client.py::test_slot_config_loading_from_json_file` (expects unknown model `claude-test` to be served), `::test_invalid_slot_config_slots_shape_falls_back_to_defaults`, and `::test_invalid_slot_config_entry_falls_back_to_defaults` (both expect fallback-to-defaults rather than fail-closed).

## Test gate

- **Named test:** `tests/test_llm_client.py::test_non_current_lifecycle_model_is_not_served` — pin `openai/gpt-5.5` via `LANGCHAIN_SLOT_CONFIG` against a hermetic registry entry with `lifecycle: "compatibility"` plus a `lifecycle: "current"` alternative; assert `create_llm` is never invoked with `gpt-5.5` (the fake raises `AssertionError` if it is) and that `build_chat_client()` does not serve it.
- **Deliberate-break → revert:** revert the eligibility check in `_load_slot_config` (`llm/client.py:87-123`) to `is_model_blocked`-only → confirm `test_non_current_lifecycle_model_is_not_served` **FAILS** with `gpt-5.5` reaching `create_llm` → restore the check and confirm it passes.

## Non-Goals

- Do **NOT** change the `blocked: true` guard semantics, and do **NOT** edit `tools/llm_registry.py` or `tools/langchain_client.py` — both are synced from `stranske/Workflows` per `.github/sync-manifest.yml` and local edits will be overwritten by the next sync.
- Do **NOT** edit `config/model_registry.json`, `config/llm_slots.json`, or any `review_by` / selection status. Model-selection changes require the Workflows paired-benchmark + human-approval path.
- Do **NOT** delete `llm/client.py` wholesale or re-route `api/chat.py` onto a new provider abstraction; keep the change scoped to eligibility enforcement plus the dead fallback.
- No scaffolding / TODO-only changes; every task above is a concrete edit verified by the gate.

_Surfaced by a fleet LLM-safety audit of the synced `tools/llm_registry.py` consumers; verified against `main` @ `e4bea37` by reading each cited line and reproducing the `gpt-5.5` divergence against the repo's real `config/model_registry.json`._
title: [P1] Chat path uses fail-open llm/client.py — registry-ineligible models (lifecycle != current) can stay primary

body:
## Why

This repo consumes `stranske-pdf-extract` but pins it to an arbitrary Workflows `main` commit SHA (`a0ee3aa25c08…`) instead of the released tag `pdf-extract-v0.1.0` (commit `ccfea351…`). Verified in merged migration PR #1393: `pyproject.toml` pins `stranske-pdf-extract[baseline] @ git+https://github.com/stranske/Workflows.git@a0ee3aa25c08d4eeb8e96dc6c8d7791930cd2d9a#subdirectory=packages/stranske_pdf_extract`. Not a current break, but it violates the distribution decision in `packages/stranske_pdf_extract/docs/DESIGN.md` §2 to pin a semver tag and upgrade deliberately. Umbrella / tracking: stranske/Workflows#2820.

## Scope

Re-pin `stranske-pdf-extract` in `pyproject.toml` from the SHA to `pdf-extract-v0.1.0`, keeping this repo's existing extras, and regenerate the lockfile(s) that embed the git URL. No other changes.

## Non-Goals

Do NOT change the package itself or move/retag the release.

Do NOT change which extras this repo uses.

Do NOT switch back to copy-sync.

Scaffold-only / partial completion does NOT count: leaving any `@a0ee3aa2` or other bare-SHA pin in `pyproject.toml` or the lockfiles is a failure.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `pyproject.toml` to change the `stranske-pdf-extract` dependency ref from `@a0ee3aa25c08…` to `@pdf-extract-v0.1.0`, keeping `#subdirectory=packages/stranske_pdf_extract` and the existing extras.
- [ ] Regenerate the lockfile(s) so their embedded git URL uses `@pdf-extract-v0.1.0` instead of the SHA.
  - [ ] Identify which lockfile format is used in this repository for requirements.txt (verify: formatter passes)
  - [ ] Identify which lockfile format is used in this repository for poetry.lock (verify: formatter passes)
  - [ ] Identify which lockfile format is used in this repository for Pipfile.lock (verify: formatter passes)
  - [ ] Identify which lockfile format is used in this repository for or uv.lock (verify: formatter passes)
  - [ ] Run the appropriate lock regeneration command for the identified lockfile format (verify: formatter passes)
  - [ ] Verify the regenerated lockfile contains the git URL with @pdf-extract-v0.1.0 instead of the SHA
- [ ] Test the deliberate-break verification by temporarily changing the pin to `@pdf-extract-vDOES-NOT-EXIST`, confirming install/CI fails to resolve the ref, then reverting to `@pdf-extract-v0.1.0`.
  - [ ] Create a temporary branch (verify: confirm completion in repo)
  - [ ] change the dependency pin to @pdf-extract-vDOES-NOT-EXIST in pyproject.toml (verify: dependencies updated)
  - [ ] Attempt to install dependencies (verify: dependencies updated)
  - [ ] verify that the installation fails with a ref resolution error
  - [ ] Revert the pin back to @pdf-extract-v0.1.0 (verify: confirm completion in repo)
  - [ ] _(2 further sub-tasks elided; split this issue)_

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn "a0ee3aa2" .` returns no hits.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` contains the `stranske-pdf-extract` dependency with `@pdf-extract-v0.1.0#subdirectory=packages/stranske_pdf_extract`.
- [ ] `tests/test_extract_pdf.py` passes in CI with the tag pin.
- [ ] With the pin temporarily changed to `@pdf-extract-vDOES-NOT-EXIST`, dependency install or CI fails to resolve the ref.
- [ ] After reverting to `@pdf-extract-v0.1.0`, dependency install succeeds and `tests/test_extract_pdf.py` passes.

## Implementation Notes

## Why
Remaining cross-reference feeds of design #1404, beyond the Form-4 slice (#1461): **short-interest** and **options** data, to further de-bias the long-only "conviction" signal (`conviction_scores`, `schema.sql:315`; signals in `api/signals.py`). Both are net-new (verified absent).

## Blocked by
**#1461** (#1461) — reuse its issuer-resolution + annotation pattern (held security → issuer → external signal → annotate conviction). Land Form-4 first to prove the pattern before adding paid/rate-limited feeds.

## Scope
Two phased feeds, each keyed to the issuers managers hold, annotating conviction/signals (not re-scoring):
- **Phase 1 — short-interest** (FINRA/exchange bi-monthly short-interest; free-ish).
- **Phase 2 — options** (open-interest / put-call; likely a paid or rate-limited source — owner confirms vendor/cost before Phase 2).

## Non-Goals
- Do NOT re-derive conviction scoring — annotate only (consistent with #1461).
- Do NOT commit to a paid options vendor without owner sign-off (Phase 2 gate).
- Graceful/finite handling (#1299); a missing feed never drops conviction rows.

## Tasks
- [ ] Phase 1: `adapters/short_interest.py` + `etl/short_interest_flow.py` → `short_interest` table (dialect-aware + Alembic + schema.sql; parity #1308); annotate conviction/signals with short-interest context.
- [ ] Phase 2 (gated on owner vendor decision): `adapters/options.py` + `options_metrics` table; annotate with put/call or OI context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Test (stubbed):** short-interest for a held issuer is ingested and surfaced as an annotation; missing data → null annotation, conviction unaffected.
- [ ] Phase 2 only after the owner confirms an options vendor; same robustness/annotation contract.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break:** removing the graceful-failure guard drops conviction rows on feed failure → test fails.

## Implementation Notes
Audit baseline: stranske/Manager-Database main @ 705e427. Anchors: `conviction_scores` `schema.sql:315`, signals `api/signals.py`, issuer resolution via `holdings.resolved_ticker` (#1374). Depends on #1461. Options (Phase 2) has an owner vendor/cost gate. Part of epic #1320; remaining feeds of #1404.

body:
## Why
Follow-on variants of design #1403, beyond the Jaccard slice (#1460): (a) an **embedding-cosine** similarity option, and (b) **crowding alerts**. MDB already computes embeddings and has `crowded_trades` (`schema.sql:333`) + an `alert_rules` model (`schema.sql:224`, keyed by `event_type`).

## Blocked by
**#1460** (#1460) — build on the `manager_similarity` table + endpoint it introduces (add cosine as an alternative basis; don't fork the surface).

## Scope
(a) Add an embedding-cosine similarity basis alongside Jaccard, configurable; (b) add a crowding alert that fires when many similar managers concentrate in the same security.

## Non-Goals
- Do NOT replace Jaccard — add cosine as a selectable basis (config), keep Jaccard default until evaluated.
- Reuse `alert_rules`/`crowded_trades`; do NOT invent a parallel alert mechanism.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add a cosine basis to the similarity computation (holdings/embedding vector), selectable via config; store alongside Jaccard in `manager_similarity` (add `basis` column or a score pair).
- [ ] Add a crowding alert rule type (extend `alert_rules` event_type) that fires when > N similar managers hold the same security above a threshold; reuse `crowded_trades`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Test:** cosine similarity of two known holdings vectors matches the hand-computed value; basis is config-selectable (Jaccard remains default).
- [ ] **Test:** a crowding scenario (M similar managers in one name) fires the alert; below threshold does not.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break:** off-by-one in the crowding threshold fires spuriously → test fails.

## Implementation Notes
Audit baseline: stranske/Manager-Database main @ 705e427. Anchors: `crowded_trades` `schema.sql:333`, `alert_rules` `schema.sql:224`, embeddings in `embeddings.py`. Depends on #1460. Part of epic #1320; deferred variants of #1403.
title: [Audit] Peer similarity: embedding-cosine basis + crowding alerts

body:
## Why
Implementation of design #1401 — backtest / signal-alpha harness to validate conviction & activism signals (turn assertions into measured return/Sharpe). Owner decision on price data: **free source (yfinance/Stooq), INTERNAL-USE ONLY** (no redistribution; revisit licensing before any external sharing).

## Blocked by
**#1463** (design #1400 impl) — a backtest requires point-in-time holdings (`holdings_as_of`). Do not start until that lands.

## Scope
Replay a signal strategy (e.g. "follow high-conviction new buys") over point-in-time holdings, entering at disclosure lag, and report return / Sharpe / hit-rate vs a benchmark. Internal harness (script/flow + stored results), not an operator UI.

## Non-Goals
- Do NOT redistribute price data or expose it via the public API (ToS constraint of free sources). Internal metrics only.
- Do NOT build an operator-facing backtester UI (separate, larger).
- Do NOT re-derive conviction scoring; consume existing `conviction_scores`.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add a price adapter (`adapters/prices.py`) wrapping a free source (yfinance or Stooq) with local caching + graceful/finite handling (per #1299), keyed by `resolved_ticker` (OpenFIGI #1374).
- [ ] Add `etl/backtest_flow.py`: for a strategy over `holdings_as_of`, compute entry (disclosure + lag) → forward returns vs a benchmark; store results in a `backtest_runs`/`backtest_results` table (dialect-aware + Alembic + `schema.sql`; parity #1308).
- [ ] Report return / annualized / Sharpe / hit-rate; expose read-only via a signals endpoint or a report.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Test (stubbed prices):** a strategy over 2 quarters of fixture point-in-time holdings + known prices yields the hand-computed return/Sharpe.
- [ ] **No look-ahead:** the harness only uses holdings/prices with knowledge/date ≤ the simulated decision date (assert via a fixture where a later-known holding must be ignored).
- [ ] Missing price for a ticker degrades gracefully (position excluded + logged), never crashes the run.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break:** allowing future-dated holdings into a decision fails the no-look-ahead test.

## Implementation Notes
Audit baseline: stranske/Manager-Database main @ 705e427. Free-source internal-only per owner decision. Depends on the as-of layer from #1400. Shares the price adapter with attribution (#1402) and activism-returns (#1405-returns) — build it reusable. Part of epic #1320; implements #1401.
title: [Audit] Backtest / signal-alpha harness (free price source, internal-only)

body:
## Why
Implementation of design #1400 — owner chose **full bitemporal holdings** (event time = as-of/report quarter; knowledge time = when we learned it). Today `holdings` is written by upsert that MUTATES rows (`etl/ingest_flow.py:317` `_insert_holdings_rows` → INSERT; `etl/edgar_flow.py:221` `_insert_holding_legacy`), and filing re-ingest uses `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` (`ingest_flow.py:257-303`). So an amendment or re-ingest overwrites prior state → history is not reconstructable and any "as-of date D" answer is unsafe. This is the **foundation** for the backtest (#1401) and attribution (#1402) bets.

## Scope
Make holdings immutable + versioned so any (manager, security, as-of quarter, knowledge-time) state is reconstructable, and add an `as_of(date)` query layer. Dialect-aware (SQLite CI + Postgres prod), on the schema↔Alembic parity gate (#1308).

## Non-Goals
- Do NOT break the idempotency (#1319) / amendment-reconciliation (#1324) behavior — reconcile with them: re-ingest of an unchanged filing must not create spurious versions.
- Do NOT rewrite consumers that only need "current" holdings — provide a "latest" view so existing callers (conviction, diff, search) keep working unchanged.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add temporal columns to `holdings` (`knowledge_time timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `superseded_at timestamptz NULL`, and a stable `version`), + a new Alembic migration + `schema.sql`; register in the parity gate (#1308). Keep `filings.period_end` as the event-time axis.
- [ ] Change the holdings write path (`etl/ingest_flow.py:317`, `etl/edgar_flow.py:221`) to **append** a new version instead of mutating; mark prior rows `superseded_at` rather than deleting. A re-ingest producing identical rows must be a no-op (content hash) to avoid version churn.
- [ ] Add an as-of query layer (e.g. `adapters/base.py` or a new `etl/point_in_time.py`): `holdings_as_of(conn, manager_id, as_of_date)` returning the authoritative holdings whose `knowledge_time <= as_of_date` and latest `filed_date <= as_of_date` per (manager, period_end) — reusing the #1324 latest-filing-per-quarter logic.
- [ ] Add a "current holdings" view/helper so existing consumers are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Test:** ingest a filing (v1), then an amended filing with changed holdings (v2); `holdings_as_of(before_v2_knowledge_time)` returns v1, `holdings_as_of(after)` returns v2; v1 rows are retained with `superseded_at` set (not deleted).
- [ ] **No look-ahead:** `holdings_as_of(D)` never returns a version whose `knowledge_time > D`.
- [ ] Existing conviction/diff/search tests stay green via the "current" view.
- [ ] Dialect parity (#1308) green; **deliberate-break:** reverting append-only to mutate makes the as-of/no-look-ahead test fail.

## Implementation Notes
Audit baseline: stranske/Manager-Database main @ 705e427. Anchors: `holdings` `schema.sql:126`, write path `ingest_flow.py:317`/`edgar_flow.py:221`, filing upsert `ingest_flow.py:257-303`, event-time `filings.period_end:33`, knowledge-time proxy `filed_date:34`/`created_at`. **Large, high-blast-radius (core-table migration) — recommend owner review of the PR before merge.** Foundation for #1401/#1402. Part of epic #1320.

_Part of epic #1320; implements #1400._

body:
## Why

Implementation of the **Form-4 (insider) slice** of design issue #1404 (options/short/Form-4 cross-reference). 13F shows only long equity, so the `conviction` signal is structurally biased. Insider (Form 3/4/5) activity on the *issuers* managers hold is the cheapest de-bias signal and needs **no new vendor**: `edgartools` (pinned `edgartools==5.43.0`, `requirements.txt:6`) is already adopted for 13F (`adapters/edgar.py:_parse_13f_with_edgartools`, uses `edgar.thirteenf`) and provides Form 3/4/5 parsing. Verified absent at `main` @ `705e427`: no `form.?4`/`insider` anywhere in `adapters/`, `etl/`, `api/`, `chains/`, `schema.sql`.

Decision resolved (was open in #1404): do the **Form-4/insider slice first** (edgartools, no new data feed); short-interest + options are deferred to #1404.

## Scope

Ingest recent insider (Form 4) transactions for the issuers of securities managers hold, persist them, and annotate conviction/signals with an insider net-direction. Phase 1 = ingest + store + annotate; do NOT re-derive conviction scoring.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT add short-interest or options here (separate slices under #1404).
- Do NOT change the `conviction_scores` computation (`etl/conviction_flow.py:compute_conviction_scores`) — annotate/join, don't recompute.
- Must degrade gracefully: an issuer whose insider data can't be fetched must NOT drop or block conviction rows (finite/robust per #1299 discipline).

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `adapters/insider.py`: fetch + normalize Form 4 insider transactions for an issuer (by CIK/ticker) via edgartools' ownership/Form-4 API (confirm the exact entry point, e.g. `edgar` ownership module, mirroring how `adapters/edgar.py` wraps `edgar.thirteenf`). Preserve a stable row contract (`issuer_cik`, `ticker`, `insider_name`, `txn_code`, `shares`, `txn_date`, `acquired_disposed`).
- [ ] Add `insider_transactions` table (dialect-aware DDL + Alembic migration + `schema.sql`, mirroring `conviction_scores`; add to parity gate #1308).
- [ ] Add `etl/insider_flow.py`: resolve held securities → issuer (via `holdings.resolved_ticker`/`resolved_figi` from OpenFIGI #1374, or edgartools company lookup); pull recent Form-4 for those issuers respecting the SEC fair-use governor (`adapters/edgar.py` `_request_with_retry`); upsert into `insider_transactions`.
- [ ] Expose an insider net-direction annotation: a derived per-(manager,cusip) "insiders net buying/selling over last N days" available to `api/signals.py` (routes at `api/signals.py:313+`) and/or as a field joined to conviction output. Read-only; no conviction recompute.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test (stubbed edgartools):** a fake issuer returning 2 insider buys + 1 sell → `insider_transactions` gets 3 rows and the net-direction annotation for that issuer is "net buy".
- [ ] **Robustness test:** an issuer whose insider fetch raises → conviction rows for that manager are unaffected (no drop, no exception escaping the flow) and the annotation is null/"unknown".
- [ ] **Dialect parity:** `insider_transactions` present on both SQLite (Alembic) and Postgres (`schema.sql`) paths (gate #1308 green).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** removing the graceful-failure guard makes the robustness test fail (exception escapes / rows dropped); restoring passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline `main` @ `705e427`. Anchors: edgartools adopted (`adapters/edgar.py:192` `_parse_13f_with_edgartools`), governor `adapters/edgar.py:_request_with_retry`, `conviction_scores` `schema.sql:315` + `etl/conviction_flow.py:compute_conviction_scores`, resolved identifiers `holdings.resolved_ticker/figi` (`schema.sql:135-137`), signals API `api/signals.py`. First slice of #1404 / epic #1320; short-interest + options remain in #1404.

body:
## Why

Implementation of the near-term slice of design issue #1403 (peer-manager similarity). MDB computes embeddings and gathers `cross_manager_overlap` for chat context (`chains/holdings_analysis.py`), but exposes **no manager-to-manager similarity surface** ("managers similar to X", crowding). Verified absent at `main` @ `705e427` (no `similar`/`jaccard`/`cluster` in `api/`, `etl/`, `chains/` outside chat-context helpers). The data is already present: `holdings` (`schema.sql:126`) carries `cusip`/`resolved_ticker` and links to a manager via `filings.manager_id` (`schema.sql:31`) + `filings.period_end` (`:33`).

Decision resolved (was open in #1403): start with **Jaccard overlap on held securities** — deterministic, no model dependency, reuses existing holdings. Embedding-cosine is a follow-on (leave to #1403).

## Scope

Compute manager-to-manager Jaccard similarity over each manager's latest-period holdings, persist it, and expose a "similar managers" endpoint. Dialect-aware (SQLite + Postgres), mirroring the existing `conviction_scores` pattern.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT add the embedding-cosine variant here (follow-on under #1403).
- Do NOT build crowding **alerts** here (separate; this exposes the data, not a new alert rule).
- Do NOT recompute or alter conviction/contrarian signals.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a `manager_similarity` table (`manager_id_a`, `manager_id_b`, `jaccard`, `overlap_count`, `union_count`, `computed_at`) to `schema.sql` and a new Alembic migration; mirror the dialect-aware DDL + indexes used by `conviction_scores` (`schema.sql:315`, `etl/conviction_flow.py:_ensure_conviction_scores_table`). Add it to the schema↔Alembic parity gate (#1308).
- [ ] Add `etl/manager_similarity_flow.py`: for the latest `period_end` per manager, build each manager's held-security set (prefer `resolved_ticker`, fall back to `cusip`) from `holdings` joined to `filings` on `manager_id`; compute pairwise Jaccard = |A∩B| / |A∪B|; upsert into `manager_similarity`. Use the consolidated dialect helpers (`adapters/base.py`, post-#1361) for placeholders/columns.
- [ ] Add `GET /api/managers/{manager_id}/similar?limit=N` (in `api/managers.py`, alongside the routes at `api/managers.py:917/1233`) returning top-N peers by `jaccard` with `overlap_count`. Handle unknown/absent manager → 404/empty per existing conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test:** seed two managers with holdings sharing 2 of 4 distinct tickers → assert stored `jaccard == 0.333...` (2/6) and `overlap_count == 2`; a third manager with no overlap → `jaccard == 0`.
- [ ] **Endpoint test:** `GET /api/managers/{id}/similar` returns peers ordered by descending `jaccard`, respecting `limit`.
- [ ] **Dialect parity:** `manager_similarity` present on both the SQLite (Alembic) and Postgres (`schema.sql`) bootstrap paths (parity gate #1308 green).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** breaking the Jaccard denominator (e.g. intersection/|A| instead of |A∪B|) fails the similarity test; restoring passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline `main` @ `705e427`. Anchors: `holdings` `schema.sql:126` (has `resolved_ticker` from OpenFIGI #1374), `filings.manager_id` `schema.sql:31`, `conviction_scores` pattern `schema.sql:315` + `etl/conviction_flow.py`, similar-endpoint home `api/managers.py`. Cheapest Tier-2 win; no new external dependency. Part of #1403 / epic #1320.

body:
## Problem

MDB's activism detection is a thin, single-form slice. The field (Diligent Market Intelligence / Insightia, 13D Monitor) treats activism as a first-class **campaign-lifecycle** dataset: multi-form (13D/13G/13F together), activist profiles, estimated campaign returns + holding periods, and a letters/agreements archive. 2025 set a record 255 campaigns. This is effectively a product line, not a feature.

## Proposed approach (for discussion)

- Model an activism **campaign** entity linking a manager to a target across filings over time (13D/A amendments, 13G, related 13F positions), with status + timeline; edgartools (#1323) already parses 13D/G.
- Layer campaign-return estimation (needs the backtest/price plumbing from T2) and, optionally, a letters/agreements document store.

## Open decisions (owner)

- Ambition: campaign-linking + timeline only (bounded, near-term) vs full parity with Diligent (returns + letters archive — large, multi-quarter)?
- Campaign-return estimation depends on the price/as-of plumbing (T2/T1) — in-scope now or later?
- Is this a priority vs the other Tier-2 bets, or a longer-horizon bet to stage last?

## Definition of done (for this DESIGN issue)

Design doc: the campaign data model + a phased scope (start with 13D/G/A campaign-linking via edgartools; defer returns/letters). No code until scope is chosen.

## Notes
Part of epic #1320 (Tier-2). Largest bet; campaign-return depth depends on the bitemporal/backtest track.

body:
## Problem

13F shows only **long equity** — no shorts, options, cash, or non-US. So the "conviction" signal is structurally biased. Unusual Whales' edge is fusing options/short data with institutional holdings. Cross-referencing 13F with Form 4 (insider), short-interest (FINRA/exchange), and options would materially de-bias conviction.

## Proposed approach (for discussion)

- Add adapters for Form 4 (insider) — edgartools (adopted in #1323) already parses Form 3/4/5, so insider is the cheapest first slice — then short-interest, then options as separate feeds keyed to the same securities.
- Annotate conviction/alerts with the cross-referenced context.

## Open decisions (owner)

- Which feed first? (Recommend **Form 4 via edgartools** — no new vendor, lowest cost.) Short-interest + options need new data sources (cost/licensing).
- How far to fuse: display-only context vs feeding a recomputed conviction score?
- Phase it (Form 4 → short-interest → options) or scope only the first slice now?

## Definition of done (for this DESIGN issue)

Design doc: feed prioritization + the one-slice scope (likely Form-4/insider) + how it attaches to conviction. Form-4 slice may be promotable to an implementation issue soon (reuses edgartools).

## Notes
Part of epic #1320 (Tier-2). Form-4 slice builds on #1323 (edgartools). High effort overall (new data feeds).


_Part of epic #1320 (Tier-2)._

body:
## Problem

MDB computes embeddings and already gathers `cross_manager_overlap` for chat context, but exposes no **peer-manager similarity / clustering** surface ("managers similar to X", crowding detection) — a natural, near-term differentiator that reuses assets already in place. No prerequisite on bitemporal.

## Proposed approach (for discussion)

- Compute manager-to-manager similarity from holdings (Jaccard on positions and/or cosine on a holdings/embedding vector), materialize a "similar managers" + crowding view, and expose via API/search (and chat context).
- Standalone: does not need point-in-time data or a price source.

## Open decisions (owner)

- Similarity basis: holdings-overlap (Jaccard) vs embedding-cosine vs a blend?
- Refresh cadence + where it surfaces first (API endpoint, search facet, chat)?
- Is "crowding" (many similar managers in a name) an alert-worthy signal or just a view?

## Definition of done (for this DESIGN issue)

Design doc: similarity definition + surface + cadence. This is the cheapest Tier-2 win — likely promotable to an implementation issue quickly once the basis is chosen.

## Notes
Part of epic #1320 (Tier-2). Independent of the bitemporal track.

## Problem

MDB tracks *what* managers hold but not *how their positions performed since disclosure* — the bridge from holdings to manager skill (WhaleScore/Novus do this). Without it, "conviction" and manager ranking are unranked by realized outcome.

## Proposed approach (for discussion)

- For each disclosed position, compute return from disclosure date to subsequent dates using point-in-time holdings + prices; aggregate to manager-level realized-skill metrics.
- Heavy overlap with the backtest harness (T2) — same price source + as-of data; consider building attribution as a view on the backtest engine rather than a parallel system.

## Open decisions (owner)

- **Blocked by bitemporal holdings (T1)**; shares the price-source decision with the backtest bet (T2) — decide T2/T3 together to avoid duplicate plumbing.
- Attribution methodology (simple buy-and-hold-since-disclosure vs contribution/weighting) — how rigorous?

## Definition of done (for this DESIGN issue)

Design doc that resolves the methodology + confirms it reuses T2's price/as-of plumbing. No code until T1 (and ideally T2) land.

## Notes
Part of epic #1320 (Tier-2). Blocked by bitemporal holdings; tightly coupled to the backtest design.

body:
## Problem

MDB detects conviction/activism signals but does not validate them historically, so they are assertions, not evidence. WhaleWisdom/Novus ship backtests + skill scores; the literature quantifies 13F "alpha cloning" (~1.6–2.1%/qtr; treat higher claims as marketing). A backtest harness lets MDB *prove* its signals.

## Proposed approach (for discussion)

- Replay a strategy (e.g. "follow high-conviction new buys") over historical **point-in-time** holdings, entering at disclosure lag, and report return / Sharpe / hit-rate vs a benchmark.
- Requires as-of holdings + a price source (new dependency — see open decisions).

## Open decisions (owner)

- **Blocked by bitemporal holdings (T1)** — cannot backtest without point-in-time data. Confirm sequencing.
- Price/returns data source (cost + licensing): which provider, and is redistribution of results acceptable?
- Scope: internal signal-validation harness only, or an operator-facing backtester UI (much larger)?

## Definition of done (for this DESIGN issue)

Design doc: strategy spec, price-source decision, metrics, and the as-of data contract with T1. No code until T1 lands.

## Notes
Part of epic #1320 (Tier-2). Blocked by the bitemporal-holdings design/impl.

body:
## Problem

Holdings are stored as a single time axis. 13F amendments (/A) and late corrections rewrite history, and any "what did manager X hold as-of date D" or backtest answer is therefore suspect (look-ahead bias). The field (vBase, IVP) treats this with **bitemporal** storage: *event time* (as-of / report date) vs *knowledge time* (when we learned it). Doing it well is genuine edge — most platforms don't.

**This is the foundation** for the backtest and attribution bets (both need point-in-time holdings). Sequence it first.

## Proposed approach (for discussion)

- Add `knowledge_time` (ingest/observation timestamp) alongside the existing report/`filed` date on holdings + filings; never mutate prior rows — append corrections as new (event_time, knowledge_time) versions.
- Provide an "as-of" query helper: latest row per (manager, security, event_time) with knowledge_time ≤ Q. Pairs with the amendment-reconciliation stage (#1324, merged) which already picks the authoritative filing per manager-quarter.
- Migration: additive columns + a backfill that stamps existing rows with a best-effort knowledge_time (filed date as a proxy).

## Open decisions (owner)

- Full bitemporal (both axes, immutable history) vs a lighter "append-only with as-of view" that covers 80% of the need at lower cost?
- Retention: keep all knowledge-time versions forever, or compact after N quarters?
- Dialect: this is schema-heavy — confirm the SQLite (CI) vs Postgres (prod) representation up front (ties to the schema↔alembic parity gate #1308).

## Definition of done (for this DESIGN issue)

A short design doc + a migration/query sketch + the two decisions above resolved, so an implementation issue can be filed. No code yet.

## Notes
Part of epic #1320 (Tier-2). Prerequisite for the backtest + attribution design issues.


_Part of epic #1320 (Tier-2)._

body:
## Why

Follow-up to the hygiene work in #1316. That issue asked to remove 5 dead functions "or justify keeping each." Three were removed (`_deserialize_json_object`, `search_notes`, `evaluate_filing_summary_completeness`), but two were **kept** with a justification that doesn't hold up on inspection:

- `etl/activism_detection.py:337` `detect_events_batch` — **no production caller**. The wired activism path uses `detect_events` (singular): `etl/activism_flow.py:26,313`. `detect_events_batch` is only referenced by `tests/test_activism_detection.py:344,357`.
- `ui/search.py:18` `search_news` — **no production caller**. `ui/search.py:main()` (line 121) does not call it; no `ui/` page or `web/` demo references it. Only `tests/test_search.py:160,176` and `tests/test_wasm_demo_build.py:50` call it.

The kept-justification is encoded as `tests/test_config_hygiene.py::test_kept_issue_listed_helpers_still_have_callers`, which uses `_has_external_callers()` — a scan that **counts test files as callers** and **excludes the defining file**. So "still has callers" here means "a test calls it," which is exactly the dead-code definition the other three removals used. Net effect: two production-unreferenced functions remain, and a guard test now actively **prevents** their removal.

Verified at `main` @ `eba93e3`: neither function has a non-test caller (same-file, cross-file, or dynamic/attribute).

## Scope

Complete the #1316 dead-code removal for the two functions the prior PR retained, and remove the self-justifying guard so cleanup isn't locked out. Prove-before-delete is already satisfied (zero production callers, confirmed above).

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT remove `detect_events` (singular) — it is the wired production entry point (`activism_flow.py:313`).
- Do NOT reintroduce `search_notes` / `_deserialize_json_object` / `evaluate_filing_summary_completeness` (already correctly removed).
- If (and only if) there is a *documented, intended* production use for either — e.g. a planned operator batch entry (`detect_events_batch`) or an offline-demo search page wiring (`search_news`) — then WIRE it to a real caller instead of removing, and keep a test that exercises that real path. Absent such intent, remove.

## Tasks

- [ ] Remove `detect_events_batch` (`etl/activism_detection.py:337`) and its test `test_detect_events_batch_returns_recent_events` (`tests/test_activism_detection.py:344`) + the import at line 10.
- [ ] Remove `search_news` (`ui/search.py:18`) and update its test references (`tests/test_search.py:160,176` and `tests/test_wasm_demo_build.py:50`) — drop them, or repoint the wasm build-test to the search path the demo actually uses.
- [ ] Remove `test_kept_issue_listed_helpers_still_have_callers` and the now-unused `_has_external_callers` helper from `tests/test_config_hygiene.py`.
- [ ] Extend `test_removed_dead_code_does_not_reappear` to also assert `detect_events_batch` and `search_news` stay absent (guard against reintroduction).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test_removed_dead_code_does_not_reappear` asserts all five functions (the original 3 + these 2) are absent; the suite is green.
- [ ] `git grep` shows no definition or reference to `detect_events_batch` / `search_news` anywhere (app or tests).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** re-adding either function (unused) makes the extended `does_not_reappear` test fail; removing it passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline `main` @ `eba93e3`. Confirmed zero production callers for both functions (prod activism path = `detect_events`; `ui/search.py:main()` does not call `search_news`; no page/demo reference). Surfaced by the implementation-verification spot-check of #1316 (`Code/Audits/Manager-Database/`). Low severity (dead-code hygiene, no behavior at risk) — but closes the loop the prior PR left open.

body:
## Why

News→manager/topic tagging is **keyword-based** (`adapters/news.py` `tag()` + `_configured_topic_keywords()`; verified — no spaCy/GLiNER/FinBERT in code at `e5764a5`). Keyword matching on RSS+GDELT misses entity variants, aliases, and context, which weakens MDB's genuine edge (news fused with holdings via the manager graph). The field uses model-based NER — `gliner` (zero-shot) with the news-tuned `EmergentMethods/gliner_medium_news-v2.1` for org/ticker extraction, optionally FinBERT for sentiment.

## Scope

Add model-based entity extraction (org/ticker → manager_id) for news items, complementing/replacing keyword tagging, plus optional sentiment. Keep it optional/offline-friendly (no hard external runtime dependency for the core pipeline).

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT remove the keyword path entirely until the model path is validated — run them in parallel and compare first.
- Do NOT add a heavy GPU requirement; use CPU-friendly model sizes.
- Sentiment (FinBERT) is a nice-to-have add-on, not required for the core tagging win.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a GLiNER+spaCy news-NER step that extracts org/ticker entities from news items and links them to `manager_id` (with confidence), feeding the existing `match_entities`/topic store.
- [ ] Gate it behind config so deployments can choose keyword vs model tagging; document the model + env.
- [ ] (Optional) Add FinBERT sentiment as a per-item tag feeding the conviction/alert layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Test:** a news item naming a tracked manager by an alias/variant the keyword map misses is correctly linked by the model path (and the keyword path demonstrably misses it).
- [ ] Tagging mode is config-selectable; default behavior is unchanged unless enabled.
- [ ] No GPU required; runs in CI on CPU within a reasonable time (or is skippable behind a marker).

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline `e5764a5`. Verified: keyword tagging only (`adapters/news.py`). Refs: https://pypi.org/project/gliner/ , `EmergentMethods/gliner_medium_news-v2.1`. Part of the expansion roadmap (R5); independent of R1–R4.


_Part of epic #1320._

body:
## Why

13F filings are amended (`13F-HR/A`), and the field standard is to **reconcile** them — keep the most recent filing per manager-quarter and supersede `13F-HR` with its `13F-HR/A` — so diffs and large-delta alerts don't double-count. MDB **ingests** amendments (`adapters/edgar.py: THIRTEEN_F_FORMS = {"13F-HR", "13F-HR/A", "13-F"}`) but there is **no reconciliation logic** (verified: no latest-per-quarter/supersede handling at `e5764a5`). So raw filings — including amendments — flow into the diff, which both noises the alerts and **compounds the duplicate-holdings idempotency bug #1298**.

## Scope

Add an explicit, tested amendment-reconciliation stage that resolves to one authoritative holdings set per (manager, quarter) before diffing/alerting.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT discard amendments — they supersede, not delete; keep provenance.
- Do NOT change the alert thresholds themselves (separate concern).
- Coordinate with #1298 (idempotent holdings) — reconciliation assumes stable filing identity.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a reconciliation step (in the ingest/diff path) that, per (manager_id, period), selects the latest filing and treats `13F-HR/A` as superseding the matching `13F-HR`; mark superseded filings so downstream diff/alerts use only the authoritative set.
- [ ] Ensure the daily diff and large-delta alerts read the reconciled set, not raw filings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Test:** ingest a `13F-HR` then a `13F-HR/A` for the same manager-quarter with changed holdings; assert the diff/alerts reflect the amended holdings once (not both filings double-counted). Current code double-counts.
- [ ] Superseded filings remain queryable (provenance preserved) but are excluded from diffs/alerts.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** disabling the supersede step reproduces the double-count in the test; restoring it passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline `e5764a5`. Verified: `adapters/edgar.py:22` form set includes `13F-HR/A` but no reconciliation exists. Refs: WhaleWisdom amendment/split handling. Part of the expansion roadmap (R4); best done after R3 (edgartools) and alongside #1298. dim-5/6 "amendment reconciliation" gap.


_Part of epic #1320._
title: [Audit][R4] Add 13F amendment (/A) reconciliation as an explicit tested stage

body:
## Why

The EDGAR client + 13F parser is hand-rolled (`adapters/edgar.py`, with its own `_request_with_retry` governor and `THIRTEEN_F_FORMS` set); there is **no `edgartools`/`sec-parser` dependency** (verified absent at `e5764a5`). `edgartools` (MIT, ~2.3M downloads, actively maintained) parses 13F-HR XML **and** historical fixed-width TXT with one call, recently made 13F parsing ~8× faster, and adds Form 3/4/5, 13D/G, N-PORT, and XBRL — coverage MDB would otherwise hand-build for the Tier-2 items (insider/activism/options-adjacent). This is the single highest-leverage adoption from the field review.

## Scope

Adopt `edgartools` for EDGAR fetching/parsing (13F first; insider/13D coverage as a follow-on), behind the existing adapter interface so callers don't change. Keep behavior equivalent or better; preserve the fair-use rate limiting.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT rip out the adapter interface — wrap edgartools behind `adapters/edgar.py`'s existing surface.
- Do NOT regress the SEC fair-use governor (use edgartools' built-in limiter OR keep the current one; don't end up with neither).
- Scope this issue to 13F parsing parity + the governor; insider/13D/N-PORT expansion is a follow-on (epic Tier-2).

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `edgartools` to `tools/requirements*.txt` (and lock) and replace the hand-rolled 13F fetch/parse path in `adapters/edgar.py` with edgartools, keeping the public adapter functions stable.
- [ ] Preserve fair-use rate limiting (verify against the existing `EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL` governor; finite-validate it — see #1299).
- [ ] Add a parity test: parse a fixture 13F-HR and assert holdings match the prior parser's output (counts, CUSIPs, values).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 13F parse parity test passes against a committed fixture (same holdings out as the legacy parser).
- [ ] Fair-use pacing is preserved (a test asserts requests are spaced ≥ the configured interval).
- [ ] Existing EDGAR ingest tests stay green.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline `e5764a5`. Verified: hand-rolled parser, no edgartools dep. Refs: https://github.com/dgunning/edgartools , https://www.edgartools.io/making-sec-13f-holdings-parsing-8x-faster/ . Part of the expansion roadmap (R3); de-risks R4 (amendment parsing) and several Tier-2 items.


_Part of epic #1320._
title: [Audit][R3] Adopt edgartools for EDGAR parsing (13F parity + insider/13D follow-on)

body:
## Why

The platform runs daily/hourly Prefect flows (EDGAR, news, diff, digest) but has **no first-class data-quality / freshness subsystem** — only ad-hoc checks (verified: no Great Expectations and no standing freshness assertions in app code at `e5764a5`). Silent staleness is a real risk on a daily cadence: a harvest that didn't land, news older than N hours, a 13F row-count that dropped, or a rising unmapped-CUSIP rate (R1) currently surface only via log-grepping.

## Scope

Add declarative, alertable data-quality assertions to the daily pipeline. Prefer leveraging the existing Prefect scheduler (SLA / late-run / artifact features) and/or Great Expectations (GX Core) rather than parallel cron logic.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT build a parallel scheduler — reuse Prefect (already in use).
- Do NOT hard-fail ingest on a soft freshness warning; route to an alert/issue instead.

## Tasks

- [ ] Define standing checks: (a) each flow's harvest landed within its window (Prefect SLA/late-run), (b) news max-age below threshold, (c) per-table row-count sanity vs a rolling baseline, (d) `unmapped_cusip_rate` (from R1) under threshold.
- [ ] Wire failures to the existing alert channels (and/or open a tracking issue), not just logs.
- [ ] Document the checks + thresholds in the ops docs and `.env.example` (thresholds as env).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test simulates a missed/empty harvest and asserts the freshness check flags it (not silently green).
- [ ] A row-count drop beyond the configured tolerance is flagged.
- [ ] Thresholds are env-configurable and documented.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline `e5764a5`. Prefect deployments already exist (`etl/*_flow.py`). Refs: https://docs.greatexpectations.io/docs/reference/learn/data_quality_use_cases/freshness/ . Part of the expansion roadmap (R2). Pairs with R1's unmapped-rate metric.


_Part of epic #1320._
title: [Audit][R2] Add data-quality / freshness monitoring subsystem (Prefect SLA / Great Expectations)

body:
## Why

13F holdings key on **CUSIP**, but there is **no CUSIP→ticker/FIGI resolution layer** in the code (verified: no `openfigi`/`figi`/`cusip→ticker` references in app code at `e5764a5`). Unresolved CUSIPs silently degrade every downstream view (diffs, alerts, search, chat context). The field standard is OpenFIGI (Bloomberg, free: 25 req/min keyless, 250 with a free key, 100 jobs/request), with a documented fallback for the CUSIPs it misses, plus an **unmapped-rate** data-quality metric so coverage regressions are visible.

## Scope

Add a CUSIP→ticker (and FIGI/ISIN/LEI where available) resolution layer via OpenFIGI with a local cache + fallback, and instrument the unmapped-CUSIP rate.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT add a static/partial CUSIP table as the primary mechanism (the failure mode being fixed).
- Do NOT block ingest on resolution failures — degrade gracefully and record the unmapped rate.
- Owner decision: whether to use a free OpenFIGI key (rate limits) — leave the key in env/secrets, not code.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add an OpenFIGI client (batched, ≤100 jobs/request, rate-limited) with a persistent cache table and a fallback path for misses; resolve CUSIP→ticker/FIGI during/after holdings ingest.
- [ ] Persist resolved identifiers alongside holdings; expose them to search/chat/diff.
- [ ] Emit an `unmapped_cusip_rate` metric per ingest run; surface it (logs + the data-quality subsystem in R2 if landed).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test resolves a known CUSIP→ticker via a mocked OpenFIGI response and records a cache hit on the second call (no second API call).
- [ ] A holding whose CUSIP OpenFIGI cannot resolve is retained (not dropped) and counted toward `unmapped_cusip_rate`.
- [ ] `unmapped_cusip_rate` is emitted per run and asserted in a test.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline `e5764a5`. Verified absent: no FIGI/OpenFIGI/CUSIP-resolution in app code. Refs: https://www.openfigi.com/about/regulations . Part of the dims 5/6/7 expansion roadmap (`Code/Audits/Manager-Database/2026-06-28-EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md`, R1).


_Part of epic #1320._
title: [Audit][R1] Add OpenFIGI CUSIP->ticker resolution + unmapped-rate metric

body:
## Why

Strategic tracking epic from the 2026-06-28 full audit's expansion/competitive evaluation (dims 5/6/7), **code-verified** against `e5764a5`. Captures the product-line bets that are genuine edge vs the field (WhaleWisdom/Diligent/13D-Monitor/Novus) but require owner scoping + eval data before they become actionable work. Full analysis: `Code/Audits/Manager-Database/2026-06-28-EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md` and `2026-06-28-05-field-research.md`.

**Verified context (do NOT re-file as gaps — already present):** RAG faithfulness/attribution eval exists (`llm/evaluation.py` + `etl/evaluation_flow.py`); pgvector is in prod; cross-manager overlap data already feeds chat. The edge to defend/extend is the citation-grounded RAG chat + news⊕holdings manager graph.

## Tier-2 product bets (owner-scoped; not 2-week issues)

- [ ] **Point-in-time / bitemporal holdings** (event-time vs knowledge-time) — foundation; prevents amendments rewriting history + look-ahead bias. Genuine edge.
- [ ] **Backtesting / signal-alpha harness** — replay high-conviction new buys, report return/Sharpe vs benchmark; validates conviction/activism signals.
- [ ] **Position-level performance attribution** — "how did this position perform since disclosure"; bridges holdings → manager skill.
- [ ] **Options / short-interest / Form-4 cross-reference** — de-bias "conviction" (13F = longs only).
- [ ] **Peer-manager similarity / clustering surface** — Jaccard/cosine on holdings → "similar managers" + crowding; reuses existing embeddings.
- [ ] **Activism as a first-class campaign-lifecycle dataset** — Diligent/13D-Monitor depth (multi-form, campaign returns, letters archive).
