## Why

A cluster of smaller, verified config/migration consistency issues (each low-severity but real; grouped to avoid issue sprawl). Sources: `Code/Audits/Manager-Database/2026-06-28-04-config-migrations.md` and `-01-correctness.md`.

1. **EDGAR governor not concurrency-safe** — `adapters/edgar.py:38-44` reads/writes the global `_last_edgar_request_at` without an `asyncio.Lock`; concurrent callers can observe the same timestamp and bunch SEC requests, violating the fair-use throttle.
2. **SQLite file default drift** — `adapters/base.py:67` defaults `DB_PATH` to `dev.db`, but `alembic/env.py:38` / `alembic.ini` default to `manager_database.db`. Running `alembic upgrade` then an ETL flow without exporting `DB_PATH` migrates one file and writes to another (silent).
3. **Non-idempotent Postgres DDL in Alembic** — matviews in `alembic/versions/001_canonical_schema.py:236-268` (bare `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`) and activism unique indexes in `006_activism_events.py:57-66` (no `IF NOT EXISTS`), unlike the idempotent `schema.sql` blocks — re-apply (partial restore / downgrade-upgrade) fails.
4. **MINIO region split** — `etl/ingest_flow.py:42` hardcodes `region_name="us-east-1"` while `api/chat.py:1401` reads `os.getenv("MINIO_REGION", ...)`; changing the env affects API but not ETL uploads.
5. **Dual Slack webhook vars** — `etl/summariser_flow.py:39` reads `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`; `alerts/channels.py:218` reads `ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`; setting one silently skips the other path.
6. **Activism timezone default** — `etl/activism_flow.py:33` `ACTIVISM_FLOW_TIMEZONE` defaults to `"UTC"` ignoring `TZ`, while `uk_flow.py`/`conviction_flow.py` use `os.getenv("TZ","UTC")` — inconsistent scheduling under a container `TZ`.

## Scope

Resolve these six consistency issues. Each is independent; address all.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change dialect-legitimate DDL differences beyond adding idempotency guards.
- Do NOT alter prod region/timezone behavior beyond making ETL and API agree.

## Tasks

- [ ] Serialize the EDGAR sleep/timestamp update behind a process-wide `asyncio.Lock` (or token-bucket) in `adapters/edgar.py`.
- [ ] Unify the SQLite default file: a single constant imported by `adapters/base.py`, ETL entrypoints, and `alembic/env.py` (or fail-fast if unset outside tests).
- [ ] Make matviews (`001`) and activism indexes (`006`) idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS` / `to_regclass` / `pg_matviews` guards) matching `schema.sql`.
- [ ] Use `os.getenv("MINIO_REGION","us-east-1")` in `etl/ingest_flow.py`.
- [ ] Unify Slack webhook resolution with a fallback chain (`ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` → `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`).
- [ ] Default `ACTIVISM_FLOW_TIMEZONE` to `os.getenv("TZ","UTC")` to match the other flows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tests: concurrent EDGAR calls are spaced ≥ interval; ingest & API resolve the same MinIO region default; activism/uk/conviction flows resolve the same TZ default; matview/activism DDL applies twice without error; `alembic/env.py` default basename matches `connect_db()` default.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** revert any one fix → its targeted test fails; restore → passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. All six source-verified (`adapters/edgar.py:38-44`, `adapters/base.py:67` vs `alembic/env.py:38`, `001:236-268`, `006:57-66`, `ingest_flow.py:42` vs `chat.py:1401`, `summariser_flow.py:39` vs `channels.py:218`, `activism_flow.py:33`).

## Why

`MAX_RESULTS_IN_MEMORY` does not bound a single large filing. In `etl/ingest_flow.py`:

- `max_results = int(os.getenv("MAX_RESULTS_IN_MEMORY", "100000"))` (line 383)
- `should_keep_results = row_count < max_results` is computed **before** the current filing's rows are added (line 420)
- when true, `results.extend(parsed_rows)` appends the **entire** list (line 436)

**Failure mode:** with `MAX_RESULTS_IN_MEMORY=100000`, a single filing with 500000 parsed holdings returns all 500000 rows in memory (the cap only gates *whether* to append, not *how many*). Also, a non-integer env value crashes the task at `int(...)`.

## Scope

Make the in-memory result budget a true cap, and validate the env value.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change DB persistence counts — only the in-memory `results` return budget.

## Tasks

- [ ] Append only the remaining budget: `remaining = max(0, max_results - len(results)); results.extend(parsed_rows[:remaining])` (around `etl/ingest_flow.py:435-436`).
- [ ] Validate `MAX_RESULTS_IN_MEMORY` (finite positive int; fall back to default with a warning on bad input).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test (currently failing):** stub an adapter to return one filing with `max_results + 1` parsed rows, set `MAX_RESULTS_IN_MEMORY=max_results`; assert `len(results) == max_results` (current code returns `max_results + 1`).
- [ ] A non-integer `MAX_RESULTS_IN_MEMORY` does not crash the flow.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting to `results.extend(parsed_rows)` fails the cap test; restoring the slice passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Source-verified at `etl/ingest_flow.py:383,420,436`.

## Why

The dual-dialect DB layer is implemented by **per-module copies** of the same helpers instead of shared functions, so every new flow re-implements (and can drift on) dialect handling. Verified copies at `e5764a5`:

- `_placeholder(conn)` / `_is_sqlite(conn)` (pick `?` vs `%s`, `isinstance(conn, sqlite3.Connection)`) duplicated across **12** modules: `etl/{activism_detection,activism_flow,conviction_flow,daily_diff_flow,digest_flow,edgar_flow,evaluation_flow,ingest_flow,news_flow}.py`, `api/{signals,chat,activism}.py`.
- `_columns` / `_get_columns` (SQLite `PRAGMA`/`pragma_table_info` vs PG `information_schema.columns`) in `etl/digest_flow.py:84`, `etl/edgar_flow.py:62`, `api/search.py:47`.
- `api_usage` table DDL in `etl/evaluation_flow.py:101`, `llm/cost_tracking.py:25`, `adapters/base.py:83/102`.
- Chain helpers: `_extract_json_text` (`chains/filing_summary.py:169`, `chains/holdings_analysis.py:155`), `_cursor_rows_to_dicts` (same two), `_guard_context`/`_acquire_connection` (`chains/rag_search.py`, `chains/nl_query.py`), `_normalize_cik` (`api/managers.py:245`, `scripts/seed_universe.py:23`, `scripts/resolve_aliases.py:29`).

## Why

The NL→SQL guardrail in `chains/nl_query.py` has two gaps (related to but distinct from the dialect-contract issue #1280 — this is the resource/safety angle):

- `_validate_sql()` (~line 137) only rejects statements whose `FROM`/`JOIN` table refs aren't in the known-tables set. A **tableless** statement like `SELECT pg_sleep(20)` has no table refs → passes validation (unless the function name happens to be a dangerous keyword).
- `_normalize_sql()` (~line 122) only **appends** `LIMIT 100` when no limit is present; it never **caps** an existing large limit, so a generated `... LIMIT 100000000` runs as-is. The Postgres `statement_timeout` (~line 153) mitigates but doesn't remove the availability/resource risk.

## Scope

Require at least one known application-table reference and cap any existing LIMIT.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT duplicate #1280's dialect-contract work; coordinate if both land.
- Do NOT block legitimate multi-table read queries over known tables.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `_validate_sql()`, require ≥1 known application-table reference; reject system/catalog/function-only SQL (`pg_*`, `sqlite_*`, `pragma`, `information_schema`, and function-only `SELECT`s unless explicitly allowlisted).
- [ ] In `_normalize_sql()`, parse any existing `LIMIT` and clamp it to the configured maximum before execution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New tests (currently failing):** `_validate_sql("SELECT pg_sleep(20)")` returns invalid; `_normalize_sql("SELECT * FROM managers LIMIT 1000000")` returns a query capped at the configured max (e.g. 100).
- [ ] Valid known-table queries still pass.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting either guard makes its test pass the dangerous input; restoring blocks/caps it.

## Implementation Notes

body:
## Why

`api/chat.py` `_build_chain()` catches **every** exception while importing a chain module / resolving its class and silently returns a fallback stub:

```
try:
    module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
    chain_cls = getattr(module, class_name)
except Exception:
    return FALLBACK_CHAINS[chain_name]()
```

**Failure mode:** a real production break (bad dependency import, init-time error, renamed class) becomes a **200 OK with generic stub text** instead of a failed health signal. Operators and callers receive fabricated success while the RAG/NL-query path is actually down. (Observed in audit: a live `/chat` call returned `chain_used:"legacy_search"` fallback rather than surfacing that the RAG chain wasn't available.)

## Scope

Restrict the silent fallback to an explicit offline/dev mode (or to narrowly-expected optional-import errors); make genuine chain failures visible in production.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT remove the offline/stlite fallback path used intentionally for the zero-egress demo.
- Do NOT change successful chain behavior.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `_build_chain()`, scope the broad `except Exception` to expected optional-module conditions (or gate on an explicit offline flag). In production, log the exception and propagate a 5xx/503 (or a structured "chain unavailable" error), not a fabricated stub answer.
- [ ] Ensure `/health` (or `/health/detailed`) reflects chain availability so outages are observable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test (currently failing):** monkeypatch `importlib.import_module` to raise `RuntimeError("boom")` for `chains.rag_search`; call the chat route for a RAG question; assert a 5xx/503 (or explicit unavailable error) in production mode — current code returns a 200 fallback.
- [ ] Offline/dev mode still returns the stub intentionally.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting to the unconditional `except Exception: return stub` makes the test see a 200; restoring the scoped handling yields 5xx.

body:
## Why

`etl/ingest_flow.py` `_insert_filing()` uses **`INSERT OR REPLACE INTO filings(...)`** on SQLite (lines ~257 and ~266) but **`ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE ... RETURNING`** on Postgres (lines ~281, ~296). SQLite `INSERT OR REPLACE` is delete-then-insert: re-ingesting the same filing **deletes the old row and inserts a new one with a new `rowid`/primary key**, while Postgres keeps the same filing id.

**Failure mode:** on SQLite, reingesting a filing changes its identity, so child `holdings` referencing the old `filing_id` are orphaned (or cascade-deleted). Same logical operation, divergent data outcome across dialects — invisible to the token-based `check_dialect_portability.py` gate and to homogeneous fixtures. (Compounds the duplicate-holdings idempotency issue in #1298.)

## Scope

Make SQLite filing upsert preserve row identity, matching Postgres semantics.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change the Postgres `ON CONFLICT` path.
- Do NOT remove the uniqueness constraints that make upsert possible.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace SQLite `INSERT OR REPLACE` with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(<unique key>) DO UPDATE` (SQLite 3.24+) that keeps the existing primary key, and return the stable id; reload child holdings transactionally against that stable id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test (currently failing):** create a SQLite `filings` row with a unique `(source, external_id)` and a child holding; call `_insert_filing()` again for the same external id; assert the filing id is unchanged and the child holding is not orphaned. Current `INSERT OR REPLACE` changes the id.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting to `INSERT OR REPLACE` fails the identity-stability test; restoring `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Source-verified: SQLite `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO filings` and PG `ON CONFLICT ... RETURNING` in `etl/ingest_flow.py` `_insert_filing()`.

body:
## Why

Two DB connection-lifecycle defects let telemetry/error paths leak connections and mask the primary operation.

1. **`adapters/base.py` `tracked_call()`** writes usage metrics in a `finally:` block: it opens `conn = connect_db(db_path)` and only `conn.close()`s inside that same block. If `connect_db()`, schema setup, `conn.execute()`, or `conn.commit()` raises, the exception escapes the context manager — **replacing the successful primary result (e.g. an EDGAR/news HTTP call) with a telemetry failure** — and on an error before `close()`, the connection **leaks**. (Verified: `finally:` at base.py:~168, `connect_db` at ~180, `conn.close()` at ~193.)
2. **`etl/ingest_flow.py` `fetch_and_store()`** opens `conn = connect_db(...)` at line 378 and closes it only on the normal path at line 442. Any raise from `download()`/`put_object()`/`parse()`/`_insert_filing()`/`_insert_holdings_rows()`/`commit()` **leaks the connection and may leave a transaction open**; the outer loop catches broad `Exception` and continues, compounding SQLite locks/partial data.

## Scope

Make metrics persistence isolated and non-fatal, and make ingest connection handling exception-safe.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT drop usage-metrics logging — just stop letting it fail the primary call.
- Do NOT change the per-filing retry/skip policy beyond ensuring rollback+close.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `tracked_call()`, wrap metrics persistence in its own `try/except/finally`; always `close()` the metrics connection; never replace the original result/exception with a telemetry failure (log a warning instead).
- [ ] In `fetch_and_store()`, use a connection context manager or `try/except/finally`: roll back on any per-filing failure after the connection opens, then close unconditionally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test (currently failing):** in `tracked_call()`, a successful inner HTTP response with a metrics-connection `execute()` that raises → returns the successful response (not an exception) and closes the metrics connection.
- [ ] **New test (currently failing):** `fetch_and_store` with an adapter whose `parse()` raises after the connection opens → connection `close()`/rollback called; a subsequent SQLite call is not blocked by a lock.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting either fix reproduces the escape/leak in its test; restoring passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Source-verified at `adapters/base.py:166-193` and `etl/ingest_flow.py:378,442`.

body:
## Why

Prod Postgres bootstraps from `schema.sql` (compose initdb mount); CI/tests bootstrap from `alembic upgrade head` on SQLite. There is **no gate comparing the two**, so CI validates a schema that differs from production. Verified divergences at `e5764a5`:

- `idx_news_items_topics_gin` exists in `schema.sql:160` but is **absent from every Alembic migration** (0 hits) — topic-array query support present in compose Postgres, missing on Alembic-bootstrapped Postgres.
- `documents.embedding` is added Postgres-only in `alembic/versions/001_canonical_schema.py:170` (`ALTER TABLE documents ADD COLUMN ... vector(384)`); the SQLite Alembic path lacks it and `embeddings.py` patches it at runtime (see related #1281) — so Alembic-SQLite schema ≠ `schema.sql`.
- `chat_feedback.created_at`: `schema.sql` declares it `NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, but `alembic/versions/009_chat_feedback.py:30` sets `nullable=True`.

## Scope

Add a parity gate that fails CI when `schema.sql` and the Alembic-produced schema diverge on Postgres, and close the verified gaps above.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT remove dialect-legitimate differences (e.g. GIN/`vector` are Postgres-only; SQLite equivalents may be skipped — but the gate must record them as intentional).
- Do NOT change the existing `scripts/check_dialect_portability.py` token gate; this is a complementary structural parity check.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a parity check (script or test) that bootstraps an ephemeral Postgres two ways — `schema.sql` vs `alembic upgrade head` — and diffs tables/columns/indexes/nullability, failing on undocumented divergence.
- [ ] Add `idx_news_items_topics_gin` via a dialect-guarded Alembic migration (Postgres `postgresql_using='gin'`; skip/equivalent on SQLite).
- [ ] Set `created_at nullable=False` in `alembic/versions/009_chat_feedback.py:30` to match `schema.sql`.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Why

`make db-seed` cannot seed a local SQLite dev database, contradicting the dual-dialect design the rest of the app follows.

- `Makefile` `db-seed:` runs `python scripts/seed_managers.py`.
- `scripts/seed_managers.py:28` hardcodes a Postgres default: `return os.getenv("DB_URL", "postgresql://postgres:postgres@[LOCAL_HOST]/postgres")`, and `:33` connects with `psycopg.connect(_db_url())` directly. It never consults `DB_PATH` and has no SQLite branch (unlike `adapters/base.py` `connect_db()`, which the rest of the app uses).

**Reproduced (audit):** with `DB_URL` unset and `DB_PATH` set to a local SQLite file, `python scripts/seed_managers.py` fails with `psycopg.OperationalError: connection ... port 5432 ... Connection refused` instead of seeding SQLite. So a developer following the local SQLite path cannot seed managers.

## Scope

Make `seed_managers.py` honor the same connection contract as the rest of the app (SQLite via `DB_PATH` when `DB_URL` is unset).

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change Postgres seeding behavior when `DB_URL` is set.
- Do NOT duplicate connection logic — route through `adapters.base.connect_db()`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Refactor `scripts/seed_managers.py` to obtain its connection via `adapters.base.connect_db()` (or equivalent) so it uses SQLite (`DB_PATH`) when `DB_URL` is unset and Postgres when set. Ensure the seed SQL uses backend-aware placeholders/DDL consistent with the dialect-portability gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test (currently failing):** with `DB_URL` unset and `DB_PATH` a temp SQLite file, running the seed entrypoint creates/populates the `managers` table in that SQLite file (no Postgres connection attempted).
- [ ] Postgres seeding still works when `DB_URL` is set.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting to the hardcoded Postgres `DB_URL` default fails the SQLite seed test; restoring the `connect_db()` route passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Reproduced by running the seed under `DB_PATH` (SQLite) with `DB_URL` unset → psycopg/5432 failure. Source: `seed_managers.py:28,33`. Note `scripts/seed_universe.py` / `scripts/resolve_aliases.py` ARE dialect-aware (per `docs/reports/dialect_portability_audit.md`) — `seed_managers.py` is the outlier.

body:
## Why

The SQLite manager-id convention is inconsistent between the API (which has a dialect resolver) and the ETL flows (which hardcode `manager_id`), so ETL breaks on any SQLite database bootstrapped by the API.

- `api/managers.py:136` creates the SQLite table as `managers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ...)`, and `api/managers.py:33` `_manager_id_column(conn)` correctly returns `"id"` for SQLite / `"manager_id"` for Postgres.
- ETL readers do NOT use that resolver — they hardcode `manager_id`: `etl/news_flow.py:71` (`SELECT manager_id, name, aliases FROM managers`), `etl/daily_diff_flow.py:138`, `diff_holdings.py:70`, `etl/activism_flow.py:124`.

**Failure mode:** on a SQLite DB created via the manager API (the documented local/dev path), ETL flows fail with `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: manager_id`. Prod Postgres is unaffected (its column IS `manager_id` per `schema.sql`), and CI can miss it when fixtures create a different schema than the app itself creates.

## Scope

Make ETL manager-id access dialect-correct so the SQLite-bootstrapped path works end-to-end.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change the Postgres schema (`manager_id` stays canonical there).
- Do NOT duplicate the resolver — reuse the existing `_manager_id_column` logic.

## Tasks

- [ ] Export/reuse a shared manager-id column resolver and apply it in `etl/news_flow.py:71`, `etl/daily_diff_flow.py:138`, `diff_holdings.py:70`, `etl/activism_flow.py:124` (and any other hardcoded `manager_id` reader of the `managers` table). Alternatively, standardize the SQLite `managers` schema on `manager_id`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test (currently failing):** in a fresh SQLite DB, create a manager via the API path (`_ensure_manager_table()` + insert), then call an ETL reader (e.g. `_fetch_all_manager_ids(conn)` / `match_entities`); current code raises `no such column: manager_id`, fixed code returns the inserted manager id.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting ETL to hardcoded `manager_id` fails the new test; restoring the resolver passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Source-verified: API SQLite create at `managers.py:136`, resolver at `managers.py:33`, hardcoded ETL reads at the listed lines. Prod-Postgres path is unaffected; this is a SQLite/local-path wiring fix.

body:
## Why

`connect_db()` can silently write to local SQLite when the deployment is configured for Postgres.

`adapters/base.py:49-67`: the Postgres branch is only taken when `DB_URL` is set, starts with `postgres`, AND the optional `psycopg` import succeeded (`:52` `if url and psycopg and url.startswith("postgres")`). If `DB_URL=postgresql://...` is present but `psycopg` is `None` (missing/broken install), control falls through to `:67` `path = db_path or os.getenv("DB_PATH", "dev.db")` and opens SQLite — with no error.

**Failure mode:** a Postgres-configured production/staging node with a broken `psycopg` install writes to a local `dev.db` file. Split-brain data; operators believe `DB_URL` took effect when it didn't; packaging failures are hidden. (Mitigated only when `psycopg[binary]` is correctly installed per `requirements.txt`.)

## Scope

Treat an explicit Postgres `DB_URL` as authoritative: never silently downgrade to SQLite.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT remove the legitimate SQLite path used when `DB_URL` is unset (local/CI).
- Do NOT change retry/timeout behavior.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `adapters/base.py:49-67`, if `DB_URL` starts with `postgres` and `psycopg is None`, raise a clear configuration error (with an install hint) instead of falling through to SQLite.
- [ ] Reject unsupported non-empty `DB_URL` schemes explicitly rather than ignoring them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test (currently failing):** with `DB_URL=postgresql://example/db`, `DB_PATH` pointed at a temp path, and `adapters.base.psycopg` monkeypatched to `None`, `connect_db()` raises and does NOT create/open the SQLite file.
- [ ] SQLite path still works when `DB_URL` is unset.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting to the silent fallback makes the new test fail (SQLite file created); restoring the raise passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Source-verified at `adapters/base.py:49-67`. (cursor config audit independently flagged this as a MINOR; codex graded BLOCKER — the split-brain data risk justifies treating it as a P1 correctness fix.)

body:
## Why

The chat rate limiter — the cost/abuse control around LLM-backed endpoints — is trivially bypassable, and is not operationally tunable.

- `api/chat.py:405` `_chat_session_id()` trusts the client header first: `:409` `header_value = request.headers.get("x-session-id")`, `:411` `return f"header:{header_value}"`. The limiter is applied at `api/chat.py:971` before any authenticated principal is established.
- **Bypass:** an unauthenticated client rotates `x-session-id` per request and never hits the 10/min budget, from the same IP. Verified the header-trust path in source.
- The limit is also hardcoded (`api/chat.py:367-368` `_CHAT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=10`, `_CHAT_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS=60.0`) with no env override, so operators cannot tune abuse protection without a code change/redeploy.

## Scope

Make the anonymous chat quota resistant to client-controlled identity, and make the limit env-configurable.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT remove the existing per-session limiter behavior for legitimate authenticated/server-issued sessions.
- Do NOT add a full auth system here — scope is the limiter identity + configurability.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `api/chat.py:405-411`, stop using a raw client header as the primary quota key for anonymous traffic. Key on client IP plus a server-issued/signed session cookie (or an authenticated principal when present). Add a coarser per-IP global limiter for LLM endpoints.
- [ ] Make limits env-configurable: `CHAT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` / `CHAT_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS` with current values as defaults (`api/chat.py:367-368`); document in `.env.example` and `docs/api_rate_limiting.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New test (currently failing):** issue 11 `/api/chat` requests from one client with 11 distinct `x-session-id` values and the same IP; expect HTTP 429 on the 11th (current code allows all 11).
- [ ] Existing `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py` updated to assert the env override is respected.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting to header-keyed identity makes the bypass test pass all 11 (fail); restoring IP/cookie keying enforces 429.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Source-verified: `_chat_session_id` header trust at `chat.py:409-411`; hardcoded constants at `chat.py:367-368`; limiter applied at `chat.py:971`.

body:
## Why

Multiple numeric trust boundaries parse external/LLM/EDGAR/env values with raw `float()` and **no `math.isfinite()` / range check**, so `NaN` and `inf` flow into comparisons and scoring. (`explainability.py` already guards finiteness — the rest don't.) Verified sites at `e5764a5`:

- `alerts/engine.py:12` `_as_float()` → `return float(value)`. A rule `{"value_usd_gt": "nan"}` fires for any finite payload (`value <= NaN` is `False`); `{"value_usd": "inf"}` beats any finite threshold; NaN ages/deltas silently suppress valid alerts.
- `etl/activism_detection.py:87` `_to_float()` and `:97` `_parse_thresholds()` accept non-finite and out-of-range percentages. Ownership `"inf"` crosses every threshold (`:333`); `ACTIVISM_THRESHOLDS=nan` yields an empty threshold set; ownership outside `0..100` is not rejected.
- `etl/conviction_flow.py:141,159` sums `float(value_usd or 0.0)` then divides — one NaN holding makes `total_value` NaN (all conviction → 0); an `inf` produces non-finite weights, which are persisted and drive crowded-trade/contrarian calcs.
- `adapters/edgar.py:25` `EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL` parsed with raw `float()`; `nan` disables the `>0` throttle check and `inf`/negative break pacing.
- `api/search.py:71,80` `_normalize_rank()`/`_vector_relevance()` — non-finite rank/distance propagate into `SearchResult(relevance=...)` (Pydantic may then 500 the whole response).

These survive green CI because baseline fixtures are homogeneous (no NaN/inf/out-of-range cases).

## Scope

Add a finite/bounds validation seam used at every numeric trust boundary above. Reject or quarantine non-finite/out-of-range values with a data-quality log; reject invalid rule/env definitions at create/parse time.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change valid-value behavior or rounding for in-range finite inputs.
- Do NOT add a heavyweight validation framework — a small shared helper (e.g. `parse_finite(value, lo=None, hi=None)`) is sufficient.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a shared finite-parse helper (e.g. in `adapters/base.py` or a `utils` module) and use it in: `alerts/engine.py:12`, `etl/activism_detection.py:87,97`, `etl/conviction_flow.py:141`, `adapters/edgar.py:25`, `api/search.py:71,80`.
- [ ] Enforce domain ranges: ownership/threshold `0..100`; EDGAR interval finite and within a sane min/max; relevance finite in `[0,1]`.
- [ ] Reject invalid alert-rule numeric definitions at create/update; reject non-finite `ACTIVISM_THRESHOLDS`/`EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL` at startup (fail-fast or explicit fallback + warning).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New tests, each currently failing:** (a) alert rule `condition_json={"value_usd_gt":"nan"}` + payload `{"value_usd":1}` → no fired alert / rule rejected; (b) `detect_events()` with ownership `"inf"` → no threshold crossing; (c) `compute_conviction_scores` with one NaN `value_usd` → raises/skips, no corrupted rows; (d) `_score_result(..., fts_rank=float("nan"))` returns finite `[0,1]`.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** removing any one finite-check makes its test fail; restoring passes.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Generalizes the Inv-Man-Intake "finite/bounds sweep" (`<0/>1` guards are insufficient — use `math.isfinite` + range). All cited line numbers source-verified.

body:
## Why

The scheduled EDGAR ingest is **not idempotent** and corrupts holdings data on every nightly run.

- The deployed schedule passes no watermark: `etl/edgar_flow.py` `edgar_deployment` sets `parameters={"cik_list": None, "since": None}`.
- `since=None` becomes `"1970-01-01"` in the generic wrapper: `etl/ingest_flow.py:462` (`since = since or "1970-01-01"`), so every run refetches the full filing history.
- For each returned filing, `fetch_and_store()` (`etl/edgar_flow.py:~300`) reuses the filing row via `_upsert_filing_legacy()` but then **unconditionally** loops `for row in parsed_rows: _insert_holding_legacy(conn, filing_id, row, ...)` — it never deletes/replaces the existing child holdings for that `filing_id`.

**Failure mode:** each nightly run appends another full copy of every holding under the same filing. Portfolio weights, daily diffs, crowded-trade/conviction signals, and alert thresholds are then computed on duplicated positions — silent, compounding data corruption. CI's SQLite path doesn't catch it because tests don't run the same filing twice.

## Scope

Make EDGAR/generic ingest idempotent: a re-run of an already-stored filing must not multiply its holdings, and the deployed schedule should not refetch all history every night.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change the dialect-portability gate semantics (`scripts/check_dialect_portability.py`).
- Do NOT silence the duplication by skipping filings entirely — re-ingest must still update changed data.

## Tasks

- [ ] Make filing reloads idempotent: before inserting holdings for an existing `filing_id`, delete/replace the prior holdings for that filing in the same transaction, OR enforce a unique holding key (`filing_id` + position identity) and upsert. Apply on both SQLite and Postgres paths (`etl/edgar_flow.py` `fetch_and_store`, `etl/ingest_flow.py` `_insert_holdings_rows`).
- [ ] Give the deployed run a real watermark: derive `since` from the latest stored `filed` date (per CIK) instead of `None`→`1970-01-01` (`etl/edgar_flow.py` `edgar_deployment`, `etl/ingest_flow.py:462`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New idempotency test:** stub the EDGAR adapter to return one filing with one holding; run `fetch_and_store.fn(cik, "1970-01-01")` twice against the same SQLite DB; assert the holdings count for that filing remains `1` (current code yields `2`).
- [ ] Watermark test: deployed-path run computes `since` from the latest stored filing rather than `1970-01-01` when prior data exists.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** removing the dedup/replace makes the idempotency test fail (count `2`); restoring it passes (count `1`).

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Verified: `since:None` in `edgar_deployment`; `since or "1970-01-01"` at `ingest_flow.py:462`; unconditional `_insert_holding_legacy` loop in `fetch_and_store`. Confirm whether a unique index exists on holdings before choosing delete-replace vs upsert.

body:
## Why

This is a **current runtime break**: the Streamlit analyst UI (`make app` / `streamlit run ui/app.py`, the `mgrdb-app` console path) **crashes on load on every page**. At the pinned `streamlit==1.58.0` (`requirements.lock:538`), `ui/app.py:15` constructs the Dashboard page with an empty `url_path` but without marking it the default:

```
st.Page(dashboard.main, title="Dashboard", icon="📈", url_path=""),
```

Streamlit 1.58 raises at `streamlit/navigation/page.py:375`:
`StreamlitAPIException: The URL path cannot be an empty string unless the page is the default page.`

Reproduced two ways (audit baseline `e5764a5`, streamlit 1.58.0):
- Live browser: loading the app shows the exception traceback, no UI.
- `AppTest`: `AppTest.from_file("ui/app.py").run()` → `at.exception` contains the StreamlitAPIException at `ui/app.py:15`.

**Why CI is green:** `tests/test_ui_navigation.py` monkeypatches `st` with a `FakeStreamlit` whose `Page()` is a no-op recorder — it never constructs a real `st.Page`, so it cannot catch the construction-time error. The real-launch smoke (`make app-smoke` / `scripts/readiness_smoke.py --launch-ui`) is **not wired into `ci.yml`**.

**In-repo reference for the fix:** the offline twin `web/wasm_app.py:29` already does it correctly: `st.Page(dashboard.main, ..., url_path="", default=True)`. The server UI builder was missed.

## Scope

Make `ui/app.py` navigation construct successfully under `streamlit==1.58.0`, and add a test that exercises the REAL Streamlit page construction so this regresses loudly.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change `web/wasm_app.py` (already correct) — that offline-demo nav is tracked separately (issue 1275).
- Do NOT downgrade or unpin Streamlit.
- Scaffold-only does NOT count: a test that keeps mocking `st.Page` is a failure of this issue — the gate must build real pages.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `ui/app.py:15`, mark the Dashboard page as default (e.g. `st.Page(dashboard.main, title="Dashboard", icon="📈", default=True)`), mirroring `web/wasm_app.py:29`.
- [ ] Replace/augment `tests/test_ui_navigation.py` with a real-construction test using `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest` that asserts `AppTest.from_file("ui/app.py").run().exception is None`.
- [ ] (Optional, recommended) Wire `make app-smoke` (`readiness_smoke.py --launch-ui`) into the CI/nightly path so a real launch is exercised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named gate passes: `python -m pytest tests/test_ui_navigation.py -q`, and the new AppTest asserts no exception on load.
- [ ] **Live verification gate:** `streamlit run ui/app.py --server.headless=true --server.port=8599` starts and the root page renders the sidebar nav (Dashboard/Daily Report/Search/Upload/Research) with NO StreamlitAPIException.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break demonstration:** reverting the `default=True` fix makes the new AppTest test FAIL; restoring it makes it pass.

## Implementation Notes

Audit baseline: `main` @ `e5764a5` on 2026-06-28. Confirmed via Streamlit `AppTest` and live browser at `streamlit==1.58.0` (matches `requirements.lock`). Root cause is `url_path=""` without `default=True`; the offline twin already carries the fix.

## Why

This is a **current documentation contract mismatch**. The top-level README says all API endpoints are subject to rate limiting (`README.md:36`). The detailed rate-limit docs say `/chat`, `/managers`, `/api/managers/bulk`, `/api/data`, and health endpoints are unlimited (`docs/api_rate_limiting.md:35`, `docs/api_rate_limiting.md:37`, `docs/api_rate_limiting.md:38`, `docs/api_rate_limiting.md:39`, `docs/api_rate_limiting.md:40`, `docs/api_rate_limiting.md:41`) and explicitly state other routes are not rate limited unless they call the chat limiter (`docs/api_rate_limiting.md:43`, `docs/api_rate_limiting.md:44`). Existing contract tests prevent this global claim in API design guidelines (`tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py:174-190`) but not in `README.md`. Missing behavior: public docs should describe the actual limited route set.

## Scope

Fix the top-level README wording and extend the rate-limit contract test to include README coverage.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change limiter behavior in `api/chat.py` in this docs-only issue.
- Do NOT add rate limiting to currently unlimited endpoints just to match the README.
- Do NOT remove the link from `README.md` to `docs/api_rate_limiting.md`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: changing the README without adding a regression test for the global-claim wording is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `README.md:36`, replace the global rate-limit claim with wording that says chat endpoints are rate limited and points to `docs/api_rate_limiting.md` for the exact matrix.
- [ ] In `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py:161-190`, add `test_readme_does_not_claim_global_rate_limiting` or extend the existing forbidden-claim helper to scan `README.md` as well as `docs/api_design_guidelines.md`.
- [ ] Keep the detailed endpoint matrix in `docs/api_rate_limiting.md:35-44` unchanged unless actual API behavior has changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Why

This is a **current policy break**. The chat API imports `llm.client` first (`api/chat.py:450`, `api/chat.py:454`, `api/chat.py:460`, `api/chat.py:463`) and only falls back to `tools.langchain_client` when `llm.client` is missing (`api/chat.py:466`, `api/chat.py:468`). `llm.client` prefers `llm/config/llm_slots.json` (`llm/client.py:24`, `llm/client.py:78`, `llm/client.py:82`, `llm/client.py:83`), whose first slot is `openai/gpt-4o-mini` (`llm/config/llm_slots.json:3`). The root model registry explicitly marks `gpt-4o-mini` as blocked (`config/model_registry.json:150`, `config/model_registry.json:156`, `config/model_registry.json:157`). Missing behavior: the runtime chat path must not select a model that the repo's approved registry blocks.

## Scope

Make `llm.client` and the `api/chat.py` chat-client path use the same approved-slot and blocked-model checks as `tools/langchain_client.py`, or route both through one shared registry-backed implementation. Keep environment overrides, slot fallback, and no-key behavior intact.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT introduce a new model registry file; use `config/model_registry.json` and `config/llm_slots.json` or the existing helper layer under `tools/llm_registry.py`.
- Do NOT remove the `llm.client.build_chat_client()` public API unless every import in `llm/__init__.py:3` and tests using it are updated.
- Do NOT make live provider calls in tests; use the existing fake `create_llm` pattern in `tests/test_llm_client.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: deleting `llm/config/llm_slots.json` or changing only a default string without asserting blocked-model rejection is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `llm/client.py:24-25` and `llm/client.py:78-90`, stop preferring the stale package-local slot file over the approved root slot configuration, or validate the package-local file through the root registry before use.
- [ ] In `llm/client.py:71-75` and `llm/client.py:96-104`, make default and loaded slots skip or reject models blocked by `config/model_registry.json`.
- [ ] In `api/chat.py:450-468`, keep the API path on the same registry-backed behavior so importing `llm.client` cannot bypass blocked-model checks.
- [ ] Update `tests/test_llm_client.py:12-22` and `tests/test_llm_client.py:24-33` so the default selected models are approved current slots, not `gpt-4o-mini` or stale Claude names.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_llm_client.py::test_blocked_slot_model_is_not_selected` that monkeypatches a slot config containing `openai/gpt-4o-mini` and asserts `build_chat_client()` skips or returns `None` rather than constructing that model.

from llm.client import build_chat_client
print(build_chat_client().model if build_chat_client() else 'none')
PY` prints an approved non-blocked model or `none`, never `gpt-4o-mini`.

body:
## Why

The repo ships a **"synthetic, offline stlite browser demo"** (`README.md:7`; run via `README_bootstrap.md:42` → "open `http://[LOCAL_HOST]/index.html`. The page loads stlite/Pyodide"). The data/compute are local (synthetic SQLite bundle built by `scripts/build_wasm_demo.py`), but the stlite **runtime** is loaded only from a third-party CDN, with no vendored/local copy:

- `web/index.html:8` → `import { mount } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@stlite/browser@0.80.4/+esm";`

Verified on `origin/main` (no local stlite assets under `web/`; no fallback). After `mount`, stlite then pulls Pyodide and the wheels listed at `web/index.html:41` (`streamlit`, `pandas`, `altair`, `pydantic`, `fastapi`, `httpx`) from the CDN/PyPI as well.

**Missing behavior:** the "offline" label only holds for compute/data — the page itself **cannot boot without internet access to `cdn.jsdelivr.net`** (and the wheel hosts). On an offline / locked-down / air-gapped PC (the Tier-A target for this fleet) the demo never mounts. With internet it works (verified in prior UX review), so this is *latent* for online use but a **current break for the documented offline target**, and each load emits an external call from the workspace.

Same class as Pension-Data #594/#596 (Plotly vendored locally), applied to the stlite runtime + Pyodide + wheels.

## Scope

Make `web/` self-contained so `index.html` boots with **no external network**: vendor the `@stlite/browser@0.80.4` runtime, Pyodide, and the wheels the demo installs, served from a repo-relative path; repoint `web/index.html` to the local copies.

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** change the demo's pages, the synthetic SQLite bundle, or `build_wasm_demo.py`'s data logic — packaging/offline-hardening only.
- Do **not** remove the demo.
- **Scaffold-only completion does NOT count for this issue:** a committed `vendor/` dir or test while `web/index.html:8` still imports from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net` is a failure. The deliberate-break acceptance criterion below must be demonstrated and the page must boot with the network blocked.
- Out of scope: the empty-default-views polish (#1214), dev-notice leak (#1215), and any theming/empty-state/error-copy work (design-system program).

## Tasks

- [ ] Vendor the stlite runtime under a repo-relative path (e.g. `web/vendor/stlite@0.80.4/`): the `@stlite/browser@0.80.4` ESM build, Pyodide, and the wheels for the packages listed at `web/index.html:41`.
- [ ] Repoint `web/index.html:8` from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@stlite/browser@0.80.4/+esm` to the vendored local module path, and configure stlite to resolve Pyodide + wheels locally.
- [ ] Extend `scripts/build_wasm_demo.py` (or add a sibling step) to fetch+place (or `--check`) the vendored runtime so the offline bundle is reproducible alongside the SQLite bundle.
- [ ] Add a static check `tests/web/test_wasm_no_external_cdn.py` asserting `web/index.html` contains **no** `cdn.jsdelivr.net` / external `http(s)://` script, style, or ES-module import.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named test gate: `tests/web/test_wasm_no_external_cdn.py::test_wasm_index_has_no_external_runtime_ref` passes — reads `web/index.html` and asserts no `https?://` in any `<script src=>`, `<link href=>`, or `import ... from "http..."`.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break → revert (falsifiability):** in `web/index.html:8`, replace the vendored import back with `import { mount } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@stlite/browser@0.80.4/+esm";` → the named test **FAILS** → revert → it passes. Capture both runs in the PR.
- [ ] Live-verification gate: serve `web/` and load `index.html` with network **disabled** (DevTools "Offline" or CDN host-block); the demo mounts and the Dashboard renders synthetic data. Capture the offline screenshot + a network panel showing zero `cdn.jsdelivr.net` requests in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Mirror Pension-Data #596 (`apps/web/vendor/plotly-*.min.js` + `tests/web/test_no_external_cdn.py`).
- Vendoring the loader alone is insufficient: Pyodide + the six wheels at `web/index.html:41` are fetched after `mount`, so the bundle must include them and stlite must be pointed at the local copies (`wheelUrls` / `pyodideUrl` style config).
- Expect a tens-of-MB bundle (Pyodide + wheels); document whether assets are committed or generated at build time.

## Why

Observed live at the top of the offline build's main pane, 2026-06-22 (HEAD `c673705`).

User-facing consequence: a non-technical operator, and anyone viewing the offline/PC demo, sees a security-flavored warning announcing that authentication is being skipped. This is confusing in a polished UI and needlessly advertises that auth is off. UX-Review panel: wired/confusion sev3, corrob 4/4 (a contributor to help_clarity 4.5 / overall 6.0, gate FAIL).

## Scope
Move the dev-mode notice in `ui/__init__.py:28` out of the primary UI by emitting it via `logging` (for example `logger.info(...)`) or a collapsed `st.sidebar` expander instead of `st.warning(...)` in the main content.

Surfaced by the UX Review (`Code/Orchestrator/ux_review.py`), 2026-06-22 — review_id `stranske/Manager-Database:uxreview:2026-06-22` (OFFLINE build). Verified at `ui/__init__.py:28` plus a live capture.

## Non-Goals
Do NOT change the auth-bypass behavior itself. Bypassing auth when creds are unset is the intended local/offline mode; only stop surfacing it in the main UI.

## Tasks
- [ ] Update `ui/__init__.py:28` to emit the dev-mode auth-bypass notice via `logging` or a collapsed `st.sidebar` expander instead of `st.warning(...)` in the main content.

## Why

In the offline stlite demo (`web/wasm_app.py`, bundled synthetic SQLite), two headline surfaces default to recent time windows that exclude the demo's data (dated 2026-03-15), so a first-time user lands on empty views with no guidance to where the data is. Observed live, 2026-06-22 (HEAD `c673705`).

Daily Report (`ui/daily_report.py:273`) defaults `date = st.date_input("Date", dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=1))` to yesterday, which renders an empty report ("Managers w/ changes 0"; "No activism events detected for this report date." `:351`; "No crowded trades detected…" `:386`) and does not point the user to 2026-03-15, the date with data.

Dashboard "Recent Activity (30 days)" (`ui/dashboard.py:1096`, 30-day threshold `:324`) renders empty Filings/Holdings/News columns because the demo data is older than 30 days, so the headline widget reads as broken.

User-facing consequence: the bundled demo opens on empty Daily Report and empty Recent Activity. UX-Review panel: workflow/efficiency_trap sev3 + help_clarity/missing_help sev3, corrob 4/4 (offline build scored 6.0/10, gate FAIL).

## Scope

Adjust demo defaults and empty-state guidance so the offline bundled demo points users to available data instead of opening on empty Daily Report and Recent Activity surfaces.

## Non-Goals

Do NOT change the seed/demo data or the 30-day window semantics for live use — adjust the demo defaults + empty-state guidance only.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update the date picker default in `ui/daily_report.py:273` to query and use the maximum filing_date from the database instead of yesterday.
- [ ] Add a "Go to latest report date" button or link beside the date picker that sets the date to the most recent available data.
- [ ] Ensure the date picker default logic gracefully handles empty databases by falling back to yesterday when no filing dates exist.
- [ ] Create a helper function to query the nearest non-empty report date given a selected date with no data.
- [ ] Update the empty-state message at `ui/daily_report.py:351` to display the nearest populated date when no activism events exist.
- [ ] Update the empty-state message at `ui/daily_report.py:386` to display the nearest populated date when no crowded trades exist.
- [ ] Make the nearest-date suggestion in empty states clickable to navigate the user to that date.
- [ ] Update `ui/dashboard.py:1096` so when "Recent Activity (30 days)" is empty it shows a sub-caption directing users to where data exists, e.g. "Nothing in the last 30 days — see Historical Filing Trend below".
- [ ] Add a test fixture that loads the bundled demo database for use across daily report tests.
- [ ] Write a test in `tests/test_daily_report_default_date.py` that verifies the Daily Report default date resolves to a date with available filing data in the bundled demo database.
- [ ] Write a test in `tests/test_daily_report_default_date.py` that verifies empty-state messages display the nearest populated date when the selected date has no data.
- [ ] Test the regression by hard-coding the default back to `today - 1 day` without a nearest-date hint, confirm `tests/test_daily_report_default_date.py` fails, then revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Daily Report defaults to a date with available filing data when opened in the bundled demo (verified by checking that at least one manager change, activism event, or crowded trade is displayed).
- [ ] When a Daily Report date has no data, each empty-state message displays text matching the pattern 'No data for this date — latest report is YYYY-MM-DD' where the date is the most recent filing_date in the database.
- [ ] When the Recent Activity widget at `ui/dashboard.py:1096` returns zero results, it displays a message containing both 'last 30 days' and a reference to 'Historical Filing Trend' (case-insensitive).
- [ ] `tests/test_daily_report_default_date.py` exists and passes against the bundled demo DB.
- [ ] Reintroducing a `today - 1 day` default with no nearest-date hint causes `tests/test_daily_report_default_date.py` to fail.

## Implementation Notes

Surfaced by the UX Review (`Code/Orchestrator/ux_review.py`), 2026-06-22 — review_id `stranske/Manager-Database:uxreview:2026-06-22` (OFFLINE build), overall 6.0/10 (gate FAIL). Verified at the cited file:lines + live captures. Fix hints from the 4/4-corroborated panel.

body:
## Why

`Manager-Intel-Platform.md:98` commits to "throttle requests (the new EDGAR rate-limits >10 rps/IP)." `adapters/edgar.py:35-58` (`_request_with_retry`) sleeps only on `httpx.RequestError` / `HTTPStatusError` during retry (line 53: `await asyncio.sleep(0.5 * attempt)`); steady-state outbound requests to `data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK*.json` (line 227) and `efts.sec.gov` (line 175) are unthrottled. A multi-CIK ingest fires successive requests with no inter-request delay, trivially exceeding the 10 req/s ceiling. The correct pattern already exists at `adapters/news.py:180-187` (GDELT `last_request_at` / `monotonic()` pacing). `docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md:31` records this as `unimplemented`. This is **latent fragility, not a current break**: single-CIK CI stubs never trip the limit, but a real manager-fleet ingest can trigger SEC IP-level throttling.

## Scope

- `adapters/edgar.py`: add `EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL` constant (default `0.11` s, env-configurable), `_last_edgar_request_at` module state, and pacing guard at the top of `_request_with_retry` before line 35's retry loop.
- `tests/test_edgar_integration.py`: add `test_outbound_request_rate_governor` that patches `edgar.asyncio.sleep` and `edgar.monotonic`, primes `edgar._last_edgar_request_at`, and asserts the shortfall is passed to sleep.
- `docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md`: reclassify row at line 31 from `unimplemented` to `implemented-and-verified`.

## Non-Goals

- Do not add semaphores or global rate-governor logic across other adapter types — scope to `adapters/edgar.py` only.
- Do not modify the existing retry backoff at `adapters/edgar.py:53` (`await asyncio.sleep(0.5 * attempt)`).
- Do not throttle `adapters/edgar.py:download()` separately — it calls `_request_with_retry` and inherits the governor automatically.
- Do not add an API endpoint or operator UI for EDGAR rate configuration.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: wiring the constant without applying it in the request path, or a test that passes with the guard deleted, is a failure. The deliberate-break gate below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `adapters/edgar.py`, add `from time import monotonic` to the import block (after line 11) and add after `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (line 23): `EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL: float = float(os.getenv("EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL", "0.11"))` and `_last_edgar_request_at: float | None = None`.
- [ ] In `adapters/edgar.py:_request_with_retry`, insert a pacing guard BEFORE `for attempt in range(1, max_retries + 1):` (line 35): `global _last_edgar_request_at`; if set and `EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL > 0`, compute `elapsed = monotonic() - _last_edgar_request_at`; if `elapsed < EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL`, `await asyncio.sleep(EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL - elapsed)`; then set `_last_edgar_request_at = monotonic()`.
- [ ] Add `test_outbound_request_rate_governor` to `tests/test_edgar_integration.py` after `test_rate_limit_handling` (line 298): `monkeypatch.setattr(edgar, "_last_edgar_request_at", 0.0)`; patch `edgar.monotonic` to return `0.05`; patch `edgar.asyncio.sleep` to record calls; call `edgar._request_with_retry` on a stub HTTP-200 client; assert `asyncio.sleep` was called with a value `>= 0.06` (the shortfall).
- [ ] Within the same test, add a `EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL=0` assertion: set `edgar.EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL = 0.0`, call `_request_with_retry` again, and assert the recording coroutine was NOT called for pacing.
- [ ] Update `docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md:31` (`Manager-Intel-Platform.md:98`): set `Classification` to `implemented-and-verified`; cite `adapters/edgar.py:_request_with_retry` and `tests/test_edgar_integration.py::test_outbound_request_rate_governor` in `Implementation or gap evidence`.
- [ ] Run `python scripts/check_dialect_portability.py` from repo root and confirm exit code 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest -m integration tests/test_edgar_integration.py::test_outbound_request_rate_governor -v` passes; asserts `asyncio.sleep` was called with a positive shortfall value (not a retry sleep).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** delete the pacing guard block from `adapters/edgar.py:_request_with_retry`; `tests/test_edgar_integration.py::test_outbound_request_rate_governor` MUST FAIL (`AssertionError`: sleep not called). Revert the deletion; test passes again. Capture the FAIL output in the PR.
- [ ] `EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL=0` case: `asyncio.sleep` is not called for inter-request pacing when the interval is `0`.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_dialect_portability.py` exits with status 0 after the change.
- [ ] `docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md:31` reads `implemented-and-verified` and cites `tests/test_edgar_integration.py::test_outbound_request_rate_governor`.

## Implementation Notes

- `adapters/edgar.py:26-59` (`_request_with_retry`): pacing guard at function start, before the retry loop; requires `global _last_edgar_request_at`.
- `adapters/edgar.py:5,7` (`import asyncio`, `import os`): both already present; only new import is `from time import monotonic`; `monkeypatch.setattr(edgar.asyncio, "sleep", ...)` and `monkeypatch.setattr(edgar, "monotonic", ...)` both work once added.
- `adapters/news.py:13,180-187`: `from time import monotonic` import to mirror; GDELT pacing pattern to copy — replace hardcoded `1.0` with `EDGAR_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL`.
- `tests/test_edgar_integration.py:272-298` (`test_rate_limit_handling`): existing `DummyClient` and `monkeypatch.setattr(edgar.asyncio, "sleep", fast_sleep)` patterns to reuse.
- `tests/test_edgar_integration.py:31-42` (`make_client`): stub HTTP client factory to reuse for the new test.
- `docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md:31`: the `unimplemented` row to update.
- `scripts/check_dialect_portability.py`: run from repo root after the change.
- `etl/edgar_flow.py`: calls `_request_with_retry` transitively; no changes needed.

## Why

Two independent review cycles surfaced the same structural problem from different starting points: authoritative design documents in this repo assert specific operational behaviors that the running implementation does not fulfill or contradicts. `Manager-Intel-Platform.md` Objective table commits to a "Nightly ETL job [that] hits the official APIs, downloads new filings, parses metadata, extracts tables, stores PDF/text," but `etl/edgar_flow.py:349-352` ends with a plain `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard — no Prefect deployment object is present. `docs/api_design_guidelines.md:11` asserts "All API endpoints are subject to rate limiting," but `api/chat.py:399` applies the limiter only to chat write paths, and `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py:82-101` pins the opposite behavior for `/managers`, `/api/data`, and health routes. These two instances were found by targeted per-issue search; no systematic enumeration across all spec docs has been run. When spec docs drift without a documented exception, analysts and operators configure the system from incorrect assumptions — the rate-limiting case directly risks misplaced backoff logic, and the scheduling gap means no operator can activate the nightly cadence the design promises.

## Scope

- Enumerate every behavioral claim in the named design/spec docs (`Manager-Intel-Platform.md`, `docs/api_design_guidelines.md`, `docs/api_rate_limiting.md`, `docs/api_changes.md`, `README_bootstrap.md`, any other `docs/*.md`) using `rg` for scheduling cadences, rate-limiting scope, SLA, and operational contract keywords.
- Classify each enumerated claim as `implemented-and-verified`, `unimplemented`, or `contradicted`, with doc:line refs and supporting code or test refs from the current checkout.
- Produce an audit report artifact at `docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md` with a summary classification table and per-claim rows.
- File one follow-up GitHub issue per `unimplemented` or `contradicted` claim not already addressed by a per-instance candidate from this review cycle.

## Non-Goals

- Do not bundle per-instance fixes into this audit PR — each unimplemented or contradicted claim ships as its own follow-up issue and fix.
- Do not widen scope to audit inline code comments or docstrings — limit to named design/spec docs that operators and analysts read.
- Do not re-audit the two already-converged per-instance candidates ("Add a scheduled EDGAR filing-ingestion deployment contract" and "Align API design guidelines with the shipped chat-only rate limiter") — cite them in the report as `unimplemented` and `contradicted` respectively with issue links.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: an audit report that lists only the two already-known instances without running the `rg` enumeration across all named docs and verifying each match against the current checkout is a failure of this issue.
- Do not implement fixes to any claim found in this audit pass — the output of this issue is the report and follow-up issues only.

## Tasks

- [ ] Run `rg -n -i "nightly|hourly|rate.?limit|all endpoint|scheduled|every day|quota|SLA" Manager-Intel-Platform.md docs/ README_bootstrap.md` and collect every line asserting a scheduling cadence, rate-limiting scope, SLA, or operational contract; record each as a row with columns: `doc`, `line`, `claim_text`, `classification`, `code_ref_or_gap`.
- [ ] For each enumerated hit, verify against the current checkout: read the cited implementation file and, if a contract test exists (`rg` the claim keyword in `tests/`), note the test path; classify the claim as `implemented-and-verified`, `unimplemented`, or `contradicted`.
- [ ] Write `docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md` with a summary table at the top (counts by classification) and per-claim rows listing: `doc:line`, `claim_text`, `classification`, `implementation_ref or gap_note`, and `linked_issue` for already-tracked items.
- [ ] For each claim classified as `unimplemented` or `contradicted` that is not already covered by a converged per-instance candidate, file one follow-up GitHub issue with the claim text, `doc:line` ref, and gap description; link each filed issue in the audit report.
- [ ] Add the audit report artifact path (`docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md`) and links to all follow-up issues filed to the PR description.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md` exists in the PR diff and contains at least two rows classified as `unimplemented` or `contradicted` (the two confirmed instances) with their `doc:line` refs and issue cross-references.
- [ ] `rg "implemented-and-verified\|unimplemented\|contradicted" docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md` returns at least 2 matches, confirming classified entries and not just section headers.
- [ ] Every claim found by `rg -i "nightly\|all endpoint.*rate limit" Manager-Intel-Platform.md docs/api_design_guidelines.md` in the current checkout appears in the audit report (no unclassified hits left out).
- [ ] Every claim classified as `unimplemented` or `contradicted` beyond the two already-tracked instances has a corresponding open GitHub issue linked in the audit report.
- [ ] The PR description contains the string `docs/reports/design-doc-behavioral-claims-audit.md` and links to all follow-up issues filed during this pass.

## Implementation Notes

- `Manager-Intel-Platform.md` — Objective table (nightly ETL commitment), Phase 1 - Production ETL table (Prefect scheduler row), Sprint backlog Week 4 (digest + SendGrid); start enumeration here.
- `docs/api_design_guidelines.md:11` — "All API endpoints are subject to rate limiting" — confirmed `contradicted`; per-instance candidate covers the fix.
- `docs/api_rate_limiting.md:28-41` — Current Endpoint Scope table; supporting evidence for the guidelines contradiction.
- `docs/api_changes.md:2026-05-09` — changelog for the chat-only contract pin; cite as provenance for the `contradicted` classification.
- `README_bootstrap.md:62-67` — "Running the ETL flow" documents only manual invocation; evaluate whether this constitutes a separate `unimplemented` claim for the nightly scheduling contract.
- `etl/edgar_flow.py:349-352` — `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard only, no deployment object; cite as evidence for the `unimplemented` scheduling claim.
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:1-17` — runs `pytest -m nightly -q`, not EDGAR ingestion; cite as non-evidence for the nightly ETL contract.
- `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py:82-101` — pins that non-chat endpoints are unlimited; cite as implementation evidence for the `contradicted` guideline classification.
- `docs/reports/dialect_portability_audit.md` — check whether it makes verified-coverage claims about Postgres CI gates not yet backed by the postgres-integration job; potential third instance.
- `alerts/db.py` — dialect-aware persistence layer (marked by the portability audit); cross-reference the audit's coverage claims against the actual CI job scope.

body:
## Why

`alerts/db.py` implements explicit SQLite/Postgres dialect branching at every persistence boundary: `is_sqlite()` (line 20), `placeholder()` (line 24), and fully separate DDL paths in `ensure_alert_tables()` (SQLite branch lines 96-147; Postgres branch lines 150-193), `insert_pending_alert()` (Postgres `RETURNING alert_id` branch at lines 296-303), `record_delivery_success()` (Postgres `text[]` update at lines 336-343), and `record_delivery_error()` (Postgres branch at lines 357-367). The portability audit (`docs/reports/dialect_portability_audit.md`) marks `alerts/db.py` as dialect-aware. Despite this, `tests/test_alert_integration.py` exercises all integration paths exclusively against SQLite — the file's `_setup_db` helper uses `sqlite3.connect(db_path)` at line 18. The `postgres-integration` CI job at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:36-63` sets `MGRDB_PG_TEST_URL` and spins up a `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` service, but its pytest command at line 63 runs only `tests/test_chain_postgres_integration.py`. A Postgres-specific regression — for example, the `ARRAY` vs. JSON serialization difference in `serialize_channels()` (lines 32-33), the `::jsonb` cast in `insert_pending_alert()` (line 298), or the partial index `WHERE enabled = true` in the Postgres DDL (line 174) — would pass all current CI gates. This is **latent fragility**: the dialect branches are implemented and appear correct, but are never exercised against a live Postgres in CI.

## Scope

- Create `tests/test_alert_postgres_integration.py` following the `MGRDB_PG_TEST_URL`-skip pattern from `tests/test_chain_postgres_integration.py:62-65`, covering `ensure_alert_tables()`, `insert_pending_alert()` + `record_delivery_success/error()`, `evaluate_and_record_new_filing_alerts()`, and `fire_alerts_for_event()` against a live Postgres connection.
- Add `tests/test_alert_postgres_integration.py` to the pytest command in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:63` so the new tests run in the existing `postgres-integration` job on every PR.

## Non-Goals

- Do not test external channel delivery (SMTP, SendGrid, Slack webhook) against live external services — `tests/test_alert_channels.py` covers delivery with mocks and that pattern is correct.
- Do not extend the `docker-smoke` CI job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:83-165`) to run ETL ingest end-to-end — that is a separate larger concern.
- Do not change alert business logic, condition evaluation in `alerts/engine.py`, or alert model definitions in `alerts/models.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a new test file where every test is skipped because `MGRDB_PG_TEST_URL` is unset at runtime is a failure — the `postgres-integration` job already sets `MGRDB_PG_TEST_URL` at `ci.yml:53`, so all tests must actually execute and exercise the Postgres branches.
- Do not modify `tests/test_alert_integration.py` — the SQLite fixture coverage stays as-is.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create `tests/test_alert_postgres_integration.py` with a `pg_url` fixture that calls `pytest.skip` when `MGRDB_PG_TEST_URL` is unset (copy the exact pattern from `tests/test_chain_postgres_integration.py:62-65`) and a `pg_conn` fixture that opens a `psycopg` connection, resets the public schema, applies `schema.sql`, and inserts a seeded `alert_rules` row for `new_filing` event type.
- [ ] Add `test_ensure_alert_tables_creates_postgres_tables`: call `ensure_alert_tables(pg_conn)` and assert both `alert_rules` and `alert_history` tables exist by querying `information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name IN ('alert_rules', 'alert_history')`.
- [ ] Add `test_insert_pending_and_record_delivery_postgres`: call `insert_pending_alert(pg_conn, fired_alert)` using the seeded rule row, then `record_delivery_success(pg_conn, alert_id, "streamlit")`, and assert the `delivered_channels` column of the retrieved `alert_history` row contains `"streamlit"` when queried with `SELECT delivered_channels FROM alert_history WHERE alert_id = %s`.
- [ ] Add `test_evaluate_and_record_new_filing_alerts_postgres`: call `evaluate_and_record_new_filing_alerts(pg_conn, filing_id=1, manager_id=1, filing_type="13F-HR")`, assert at least one `alert_id` is returned, and verify the `alert_history` row in Postgres has `event_type = 'new_filing'` and the correct `rule_id`.
- [ ] Add `test_fire_alerts_for_event_records_streamlit_channel`: call `fire_alerts_for_event(pg_conn, event, channels={"streamlit": mock_streamlit_channel})` where the mock returns `DeliveryResult(success=True, channel="streamlit", skipped=False)`, and assert returned alert_ids are non-empty and the `alert_history` row's `delivered_channels` contains `"streamlit"`.
- [ ] Update `.github/workflows/ci.yml:63`: change `pytest tests/test_chain_postgres_integration.py -v` to `pytest tests/test_chain_postgres_integration.py tests/test_alert_postgres_integration.py -v`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `MGRDB_PG_TEST_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@[LOCAL_HOST]/postgres pytest tests/test_alert_postgres_integration.py -v` passes against a live Postgres instance, with a collected count of at least 4 test functions (not 0 collected, not all-skipped).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily comment out the Postgres branch of `ensure_alert_tables()` in `alerts/db.py` (lines 150-193) so the function exits after the SQLite-only block for all connections. The test `test_ensure_alert_tables_creates_postgres_tables` must FAIL because the Postgres DDL is never executed. Revert the change; the test passes. Capture the failure in the PR.
- [ ] `rg "test_alert_postgres_integration" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns at least one match after the `ci.yml:63` update.
- [ ] All existing tests in `tests/test_alert_integration.py` still pass: `pytest tests/test_alert_integration.py -q` exits 0 with no modifications to that file.
- [ ] The `postgres-integration` CI job passes on a PR that includes these changes (CI run log confirms both test files were collected and passed).

## Implementation Notes

- `alerts/db.py:20-26` — `is_sqlite()` and `placeholder()` dialect detection helpers used throughout; understand these before writing fixtures.
- `alerts/db.py:95-193` — `ensure_alert_tables()` with separate SQLite (lines 96-147) and Postgres (lines 150-193) DDL paths; Postgres uses `bigserial`, `jsonb`, `timestamptz`, `text[]`.
- `alerts/db.py:276-304` — `insert_pending_alert()` Postgres branch uses `RETURNING alert_id` to get the primary key; verify the returned ID is a positive integer.
- `alerts/db.py:320-343` — `record_delivery_success()` Postgres branch writes to `text[]` column directly; SQLite serializes to JSON string — the key dialect difference to verify.
- `alerts/integration.py:71-91` — `evaluate_and_record_new_filing_alerts()` convenience wrapper; call this in the evaluate test.
- `alerts/integration.py:94-104` — `fire_alerts_for_event()` calls `AlertEngine(conn).evaluate()` then `AlertDispatcher.dispatch()`.
- `alerts/dispatch.py:27-43` — `dispatch_single()` calls `insert_pending_alert` then delivers channels; use a mock `NotificationChannel` to avoid external delivery in the Postgres test.
- `tests/test_chain_postgres_integration.py:61-66` — `pg_url` + `pg_conn` fixture pattern to replicate; the skip-when-unset behavior is critical.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:53` — `MGRDB_PG_TEST_URL` is already set in the `postgres-integration` job; no job-level env changes needed.
- `schema.sql` — must be applied in the `pg_conn` fixture to create the `managers` table before inserting alert rules with a `manager_id` foreign key.
- `alerts/models.py` — `AlertRule`, `FiredAlert`, `AlertEvent` needed for fixture construction.
- `alerts/channels.py` — `DeliveryResult`, `NotificationChannel` needed for the mock channel in the fire test.

body:
## Why

`docs/api_design_guidelines.md:11` states "All API endpoints are subject to rate limiting to ensure fair usage and system stability." The shipped implementation contradicts this: `api/chat.py:367-399` defines `InMemoryChatRateLimiter` and the module-level `CHAT_RATE_LIMITER`, applied exclusively to `POST /api/chat`, `POST /api/chat/*`, and `POST /api/chat/feedback`. `docs/api_rate_limiting.md` (Current Endpoint Scope table, lines 29-41) explicitly marks `/managers`, `/api/data`, and all health routes as unlimited. `docs/api_changes.md:2026-05-09` documents when the chat-only contract was pinned and confirmed. `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py::test_documented_endpoints_do_not_emit_rate_limit_headers` asserts that `GET /managers`, `GET /api/data`, and health endpoints neither return 429 nor emit rate-limit response headers (lines 82-101). No test currently prevents `docs/api_design_guidelines.md` from reverting the "all endpoints" claim. This is **latent fragility**: an API consumer reading only the guideline will implement unnecessary backoff for `/managers`, and an agent tasked with "enforcing the rate-limiting design contract" could wrongly extend the limiter to non-chat routes.

## Scope

- Edit `docs/api_design_guidelines.md:11` to replace the blanket "all endpoints" sentence with a scoped statement that delegates to `docs/api_rate_limiting.md`.
- Add one documentation-contract assertion to `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py` that reads `docs/api_design_guidelines.md` at runtime and fails if an all-endpoints claim is reintroduced, preventing silent reversion.
- No behavioral change to `api/chat.py` or any other endpoint.

## Non-Goals

- Do not implement global rate limiting — that is a product decision not made in this cycle.
- Do not change the documented bare 429 response shape (`{"detail": "Rate limit exceeded"}`) or alter how `api/chat.py` applies the chat limiter.
- Do not modify `docs/api_rate_limiting.md` or `docs/api_changes.md` — both correctly document the current contract and require no behavioral update.
- Do not extend the rate limiter to `GET /managers` or any other non-chat route as a side-effect of this doc fix.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding the test assertion without actually fixing `docs/api_design_guidelines.md`, so the test only passes because the doc was not changed, is a failure. The deliberate-break acceptance criterion below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `docs/api_design_guidelines.md`, replace the sentence at line 11 ("All API endpoints are subject to rate limiting to ensure fair usage and system stability.") with: "Rate limiting applies to the chat write paths documented in [API Rate Limiting](api_rate_limiting.md). Other endpoints are currently unlimited unless they explicitly delegate to the chat rate limiter in `api/chat.py`."
- [ ] Add `test_api_design_guidelines_do_not_claim_global_rate_limiting` to `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py` after the existing `test_rate_limit_document_matches_shipped_header_contract` (currently ending at line 172): read `REPO_ROOT / "docs/api_design_guidelines.md"`, assert its lowercased text does not contain `"all api endpoints are subject to rate limit"`, with a failure message pointing to the required replacement wording.
- [ ] Run `pytest tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py -q` and confirm all 4 existing tests plus the new assertion pass with no modifications to `api/chat.py`.
- [ ] Confirm `rg -i "all api endpoints are subject to rate limit" docs/api_design_guidelines.md` returns zero matches after the edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py::test_api_design_guidelines_do_not_claim_global_rate_limiting -q` passes after the doc edit and fails (AssertionError) with the original `docs/api_design_guidelines.md` text.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily revert `docs/api_design_guidelines.md:11` to "All API endpoints are subject to rate limiting." The new test must FAIL. Restore the corrected text; the test passes. Capture the AssertionError message in the PR.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py -q` passes in full (all existing tests plus the new assertion) with no modifications to `api/chat.py` or `docs/api_rate_limiting.md`.
- [ ] `rg -i "all.*endpoint.*rate limit" docs/api_design_guidelines.md` returns no matches.
- [ ] `docs/api_design_guidelines.md` Rate limiting section contains a link or reference to `api_rate_limiting.md`.

## Implementation Notes

- `docs/api_design_guidelines.md:9-13` — Rate limiting section; the offending sentence is on line 11.
- `docs/api_rate_limiting.md:28-41` — Current Endpoint Scope table; the authoritative contract the guideline should delegate to.
- `docs/api_changes.md:2026-05-09` — changelog for the chat-only contract pin; add a new entry here only if the behavioral contract changes (it does not in this fix).
- `api/chat.py:367-399` — `InMemoryChatRateLimiter` definition and `CHAT_RATE_LIMITER` instance; no changes needed.
- `api/managers.py:1-220` — unlimited endpoint; confirmed by absence of any `CHAT_RATE_LIMITER` reference in this file.
- `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py:23` — `REPO_ROOT` is already defined as `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`; reuse it in the new assertion to read the guideline doc.
- `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py:161-172` — `test_rate_limit_document_matches_shipped_header_contract`; the new test follows this pattern but targets `api_design_guidelines.md` instead of `api_rate_limiting.md`.
- `tests/test_rate_limit_contract.py:82-101` — `test_documented_endpoints_do_not_emit_rate_limit_headers`; no changes needed, but confirms /managers and /health are already tested as unlimited.
